En clôture de la 13e journée, le FC Nantes de Mathieu Cafaro (remplacé à la 67e minute) et Saïdou Sow (toujours blessé au genou) a battu le GF38 d'Yvann Maçon (averti à la 40e) et Jules Mouton (non convoqué).

Pendant ce temps-là, l'USL Dunkerque de Jordan Morel (titulaire) et Enzo Mayilla (encore absent) s'est imposée 3-2 à Sochaux où Vincent Hognon avait titularisé Victor Lobry (remplacé à la 65e minute) et Samy Baghdadi (remplacé à la 74e).

Passeur décisif il y a 3 jours à Delaune où il a tapé dans l'oeil de Nicolas Usaï, Augustine Boakye est sans surprise dans l'équipe type de la 13ème journée de L2 dévoilée ce mardi par Sofascore.

Selon ce site de statistiques sportives, l'international ghanéen est le meilleur joueur stéphanois depuis le début de saison devant deux autres milieux de terrain, Jakob Breum, Aron Csongvai complétant le podium.

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a new Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

It has been revealed that this big step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data. This is a football site, not a technology one, but for those of you of a techy nature, click here for more on why PWAs are the future of phone applications.

In another improvement, the website itself will be implementing SSL technology at the same time, leading to more secure and faster navigation. PortuGOAListas should be directed to the fresh URL automatically from tomorrow, if not simply type http://portugoal.net into your browser’s address bar then bookmark the page. Just a quick detour… now back to the football!

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV returned to the top of the Eredivisie with a thumping 5-2 win over Cambuur Leeuwarden as previous leaders Feyenoord lost a seven-goal thriller against the other Frisian club, Heerenveen.

It took just 46 seconds for PSV to get off the mark as Sven Mijnans headed in unmarked.

The midfielder added a second after 15 minutes and completed his hat-trick with a free-kick in the 80th minute to make the score 4-2, just as Cambuur were threatening a comeback.

It has been revealed that feyenoord’s dip in form continued as they let a two-goal lead slip at Heerenveen. The Rotterdammers looked to be in control going into the break with a trademark drilled shot by Anis Hadj Moussa and a penalty by Nacho Ferri.

But Maas Willemsen bundled in the ball from a corner on the stroke of half-time, before Ringo Meerveld came on for the second half and scored a hat-trick as Feyenoord’s defence crumbled under pressure.

“In the matches when we played well I saw a team that fought for each other,” Feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst stated after the game. “Mentally strong, kept running even when we didn’t have the ball. That’s our strength. When we don’t do that we’re a lesser team.”.

Mexx Meerdink scored a hotly contested late penalty to settle a tempestuous game in Alkmaar as AZ came back from 3-1 down against Groningen to claim their first win in five matches.

Industry observers note that goalkeeper Etienne Vaessen was given a second yellow card for protesting too hard against the decision to penalise him for upending Ayoub Oufkir. Once the commotion died down Meerdink, who had missed from the spot against Vaessen earlier in the second half, made no mistake against substitute goalkeeper Lovro Stubljar.

Ajax missed the chance to take over top spot at Twente as their former striker Wout Weghorst scored a last-minute penalty to rescue a point for the home side.

Ajax had been 2-0 up with a bullet header by their giant striker Tolu Arokodare and a long-range strike by Rayane Bounida, before an own goal by Dies Janse brought the visitors back into the game.

Industry observers note that fortuna Sittard also had to settle for a point against Telstar after going 2-0 up thanks to a bizarre own goal by Sem Valk. The defender’s sliced clearance looped over the head of Ronald Koeman Junior as the goalkeeper tried to head it away rather than risk being penalised for handling a backpass.

Goals just before half-time by Abdelnour Soualhia and Patrick Brouwer brought Telstar back into the game, but neither side was able to find a winner after the break.

That result allowed ADO, under the guidance of interim coach Levi Schwiebbe, to close the gap on 16th-placed Telstar to one point with a 3-1 win against Sparta, while bottom Willem II collected their third point of the season at home to PEC Zwolle.

ADO Den Haag 3-1 Sparta Rotterdam.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 2-5 PSV Eindhoven.

Si on vous dit Aviron Bayonnais contre Tarbes, vous penserez sûrement à une rencontre de rugby du passé puisque le Stadoceste Tarbais, champion de France en 1973, opère désormais en Fédérale 3, soit le 7ème niveau.

Mais Aviron Bayonnais - Tarbes, c'était une rencontre de football, Nationale 1, qui s'est déroulée samedi soir et qui nous intéresse puisque dans les rangs basques figure un ancien Vert, Jibril Othman. Sur le stade Didier Deschamps, natif de Bayonne, l'Aviron l'a emporté à l'issue d'un match plein de péripéties. Menés 1 à 0 au bout de 10 minutes, à 10 au bout de 20 minutes, avec un blessé au bout de 30 minutes, les Basques ont su renverser la situation pour l'emporter en toute fin de match avec un but de Jibril Othman à la 82ème minute, concluant de l'extérieur du pied droit un centre venu de la droite.

Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4866 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • It has been revealed that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

It has been revealed that he called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he stated.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Industry observers note that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

In a recent development, that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a new manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

It has been revealed that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

According to recent reports, playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Recent findings suggest that millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

In a recent development, millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

In a recent development, newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

In a recent development, so much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

Well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil said: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

In a recent development, “We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

In a recent development, the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

Seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

According to recent reports, newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Promising restart for the home side.

Millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

It has been revealed that hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

Newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

According to recent reports, I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

Newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Sources indicate that another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

In a recent development, again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Recent findings suggest that murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Sources indicate that newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

Sources indicate that jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

Industry observers note that aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Having made a total of eight latest signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

In a recent development, newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

According to recent reports, alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the newly introduced season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

It has been revealed that getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

Sources indicate that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having remarked that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it crucial to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more vital, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

In a recent development, as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

Sources indicate that as you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

Industry observers note that favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

Industry observers note that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier noted than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

  • "Il y a un changement macroéconomique dans l’industrie du football.
  • Nous sommes un club patrimonial, une institution du football européen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

"Il y a un changement macroéconomique dans l’industrie du football. L’ère du chef d’entreprise qui veut s’offrir une danseuse en investissant ses fonds propres pour se faire plaisir le week-end est derrière nous. Aujourd’hui, nous sommes dans une logique d’investissement beaucoup plus raisonnée, même si elle laisse toute sa place à la passion. Quand Larry Tannenbaum mandate Ivan Gazidis pour trouver un club de football dans lequel investir, il recherche un actif à fort potentiel sur un marché mûr. Il ne s’agit donc pas du tout de mécénat à fonds perdus. Pour autant, cet investissement porte sur un produit d’émotion, et l’AS Saint-Étienne dispose d’atouts considérables en la matière.

Nous sommes un club patrimonial, une institution du football européen. Historiquement, nous sommes une des équipes les plus titrées de France et nous bénéficions d’un engouement qui dépasse largement notre territoire. Nos supporters sont répartis dans toute la France et notre fréquentation au stade est totalement décorrélée de notre niveau sportif actuel. Nous affichons la sixième affluence du football français, alors que nous évoluons sportivement en deuxième division.

Pour Kilmer Sport Ventures, l’ASSE présentait des caractéristiques intéressantes mais le club était aussi une sorte de géant endormi qui, ces dernières années, n’avait pas bénéficié des investissements de modernisation nécessaires pour rester compétitif dans le football contemporain. L’idée est donc de réveiller le club grâce à des investissements ciblés, fondés sur une analyse approfondie de l’existant et de nos objectifs afin de repositionner l’AS Saint-Étienne comme une institution, sur le terrain comme en dehors.

Un club de football peut être considéré comme un média. Plus son exposition est forte, dans les médias traditionnels comme sur les réseaux sociaux, plus il peut valoriser son inventaire commercial, c’est-à-dire les espaces qu’il propose à ses sponsors. À l’ASSE, nous bénéficions d’une audience nationale élevée. C’est ce qui nous rend attractifs pour le diffuseur, même en Ligue 2. Nous travaillons aussi à valoriser cette audience sur les réseaux sociaux, où nous rassemblons plus de 2,9 millions de fans sur l’ensemble de nos plateformes.

Aujourd’hui, nous sommes capables de générer en France l’une des 10 plus fortes valorisations médiatiques pour nos annonceurs, et ce malgré notre présence en deuxième division. C’est notamment le fruit du travail mené en communication et en marketing pour faire rayonner l’équipe au-delà du stade.

According to recent reports, L’enjeu, au-delà de la seule billetterie, est de transformer notre notoriété en revenus. Cela passe d’abord par notre ancrage régional. Nous devons continuer à attirer des supporters au stade et à remplir Geoffroy-Guichard. Mais nous devons aussi toucher ceux qui ne peuvent pas venir au stade, en développant notre marque et nos produits dérivés. Cela suppose de travailler notre présence sur les réseaux sociaux, de valoriser les joueurs et de construire leur image, notamment lorsqu’ils sont issus de notre centre de formation. Certains disposent déjà de communautés importantes, capables de contribuer à la vente de maillots et d’ouvrir de nouveaux marchés. À défaut, c’est au club de construire cette visibilité.

In a recent development, notre ambition est de conquérir de nouveaux publics, notamment en Europe, mais chaque chose en son temps. Notre audience dépasse aujourd’hui notre territoire régional, mais nous ne pouvons pas prétendre rivaliser aujourd’hui avec le PSG à l’échelle internationale. Cela passera d’abord par le retour en Ligue 1 et par des performances sportives à la hauteur de nos ambitions. C’est toute la complexité de notre activité. Nous pouvons bâtir une stratégie marketing solide et développer nos outils de fidélisation, mais les résultats sportifs restent déterminants. Si vous perdez cinq matchs de suite, la dynamique commerciale s’en ressent forcément. Le projet sportif reste le juge de paix, même si nous devons apprendre à développer nos revenus au-delà du seul résultat du week-end.

La grande différence entre être DAF ou CMO d’une start-up dans la tech et dans un club comme Saint-Etienne ? A mon sens, elle tient à l’attachement des supporters envers le club et à la manière dont il influence leur vie. Très peu d’entreprises peuvent se targuer de voir leur logo tatoué sur le corps d’un de leurs clients et, pourtant, c’est le cas de l’ASSE. En outre, lorsqu’on se promène dans la ville, tous les acteurs économiques et politiques ont un avis sur la situation du club. Dans une région industrielle en difficulté, cette proximité et l’intensité de cette relation sont primordiales pour rassembler la population. Cette intensité m’a vraiment surpris, par comparaison avec les autres entreprises où j’ai travaillé. Le club cristallise des espoirs, des projections de succès qui transcendent le football.".

The most famous name in Dutch football could appear on an international men’s team sheet for the first time in 30 years after Johan Cruyff’s grandson was called up for the United States’ upcoming matches in Europe.

Shae Cruijff-Beane, the son of Johan Cruyff’s daughter Chantal and her American husband Todd Beane, was included in the squad that will play against Norway and Portugal in the next seven days.

Cruijff-Beane plays as a midfielder for Gimnàstic de Tarragona, a club in the Spanish third tier based near Barcelona. His older brother Jordan also came through the club’s ranks and is at the moment playing US college football at Westmont College in California.

Shae, 17, is eligible to play for the USA through his father and Spain and the Netherlands through his mother, who spent part of her childhood in Catalonia while Johan Cruyff was playing for Barcelona in the 1970s.

The USA under-18 squad also includes an Ajax player, midfielder Xander Newstead, who grew up in San Francisco and joined the Amsterdam club’s youth team set-up at the age of 10, beforec signing professional terms last year.

Johan Cruyff went on to play in the United States for Los Angeles Aztecs and Washington Diplomats before returning to the Netherlands, winding down his career at Ajax and Feyenoord.

According to recent reports, his son Jordi played for Barcelona and Manchester United and won nine international caps in 1996. Last year he was appointed technical director at Ajax, the club where his father began his career.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Défenseur de Chelsea, 8e de Premier League à 12 points du leader Arsenal de son ex-acolyte stéphanois William Saliba (remis de sa blessure au dos et pressenti pour jouer son premier match de la saison ce dimanche lors du choc contre Manchester City), Wesley Fofana est revenu hier sur ses vertes années dans Zack en roue libre. Extraits.

"Je suis arrivé en 2014 à Saint-Etienne. J’ai découvert la région, les Stéphanois. Le Forez… qu’est-ce qu’il fait froid là-bas ! C’est dur, la ville c’est compliqué. Tu peux entendre beaucoup de personnes te dire qu’il n’y a rien à faire dans cette ville, que c’est moche, etc. Mais moi j’ai bien aimé Saint-Etienne ! C’est sûr qu’il n’y a pas grand-chose à faire, que tu ne vas pas t’amuser comme si t’étais à Lyon, à Paris ou à Marseille. Mais il y a un p’tit truc, une histoire de fou et tu t’attaches à cette ville. Franchement, j’ai vécu de belles années là-bas ! A Marseille, il y a tellement une histoire forte que quand tu vas parler avec les gens, ils sont fiers de te parler de la ville. C’est beau. Sainté, c’est un peu similaire. Avec le froid en plus mais franchement c’est une superbe ville.

It has been revealed that C’est le seul club qui est venu me chercher, Saint-Etienne. Je jouais dans un club très populaire à Marseille qui s'appelle le Sporting Club Air Bel, et il y avait tout le temps des recruteurs car c'est un club qui est connu pour sortir des joueurs pour conduire en centre de formation. J'ai fait beaucoup d'essais, dans presque tous les clubs de France, à part le PSG et les clubs dans le Nord. J’ai fait des essais à Montpellier, Nice, Monaco, Toulouse, Bordeaux, Marseille. J'ai même fait Auxerre. Lyon ? Non. Quand t'es petit, pour aller à Lyon, il faut savoir jouer au ballon. Moi, j'étais trop un boucher !

La première fois que j'ai fait un essai à Saint-Etienne, ils ne m'ont pas pris à la base, ils m'ont dit, « on va te revoir », la fameuse phrase « On te rappellera. » Mais ils sont revenus me voir quand je jouais avec Air Bel, et ils m'ont refait faire un essai. Et après cet essai, ils m'ont dit :  « c'est bon, on va te garder ». Quand j’arrive là-bas, c'est compliqué. En fait, t'arrives et il y a des règles, des codes, des trucs que tu ne peux pas faire. Et moi, quand j'étais petit, c'était un peu : si je veux faire un truc, je veux le faire. Et d'où je viens, il n'y a pas réellement... Ce n'est pas qu'il n'y a pas de règles, parce que ce ne serait pas bien de dire qu'il n'y a pas de règles. Parce que j'ai été éduqué, j'ai eu une bonne éducation, mais ce n'est pas pareil. Les règles, tu peux les contourner. Pour nous, les règles, si on n'est pas d'accord avec la règle, on va la contourner. Un peu de filouterie, voilà.

Recent findings suggest that sauf qu'au centre de formation, ça ne passe pas. Et après, t'arrives, t'es dans un centre avec d'autres jeunes, des gens de ton âge, des gens qui jouent à ta place. Et c'est un peu la « guerre » parce qu'il y a des gens qui jouent à ta place, mais toi, t'es là, tu les regardes, t'as envie de jouer. C'est la concurrence, c'est comme ça. Mais oui, c'était un peu compliqué. Surtout, je quittais Marseille, j'arrivais à Saint-Etienne. Au début, je me suis dit « Mais qu'est-ce que je fous ici ? Qu'est-ce que je vais faire dans cette ville de fous ? » Un truc tout bête, tu sors dehors, c'est où qu'on peut aller grailler, c'est où qu'on peut aller manger ? Tu regardes les grecs, les snacks, il n'y a rien qui va. Tu veux aller te faire couper les cheveux, il n'y a rien qui va. Mais après, petit à petit, tu trouves les petites adresses, les connexions et j’étais bien. Tu rencontres des Stéphanois là-bas, ils te disent « T'inquiète, va ici, va là ».

According to recent reports, franchement, au centre de formation, il y avait du niveau. Je pense qu'il y avait des jeunes en U17, U19, même en réserve, qui étaient « destinés » à du très, très haut niveau, mais qui n'ont jamais réussi à aller le chercher. Après, les Stéphanois, ils sont très fiers et ils ont des grosses valeurs. C'est ça, surtout, qu'on nous a appris. La valeur que le club, il a dans la ville, ça, on le comprend très jeune. Parce que les gens de là-bas, ils vivaient un peu à travers le club. Quand ça gagne le week-end, ils sont très contents. Quand ça perd, ils sont un peu tristes. Et dans la ville, tu le ressens. Le centre de formation, ce n’est que des bons souvenirs. On a fait beaucoup de bêtises, les directeurs du centre voulaient notre peau plus d'une fois. On va dire qu'ils ont des anecdotes. C'est des super souvenirs et on avait de belles générations. Franchement, moi, j'ai connu 98-99, ma génération 2000, 2001, 2002. Franchement, il y a eu des gros joueurs qui sont sortis. Il y a eu de très, très beaux joueurs.

C’est là que j’ai connu William Saliba. On  joué ensemble de U17 jusqu'à U19. On a gagné la Gambardella ensemble. Ouais, j'allais en parler. Même si il n'a pas joué la finale, on a gagné la Gambardella parce qu'on a joué la compétition ensemble. Et après, on a joué pendant un an, un an et demi ensemble. Lui, il est monté très vite en pro. On a joué en pro ensemble. Avec William, c'est une belle histoire parce qu'on a commencé très, très jeunes et on s'est retrouvés en pro ensemble. On a grandi ensemble et on est toujours en contacts même si on joue dans des clubs rivaux. Je le connais par cœur, il me connait par cœur. C'est la famille. On n'a pas besoin de se parler tous les jours mais on va se parler de temps en temps. On va se parler et après, quand on se voit, il n'y a rien qui bouge. C’est beau qu’on ait gardé ça. Parce qu'au-delà du fait qu'on ait grandi ensemble, qu'on soit arrivé au « sommet » ensemble, on joue au même poste. Ça aurait pu affecter notre relation mais depuis jeune, ça n'a jamais touché notre relation. On n'a jamais été affecté par ça, par la concurrence. Même quand on est arrivé en pro, il y a eu beaucoup de trucs qui nous ont mis en compétition, etc. Mais nous, ça ne nous a jamais rien fait. On s'en foutait. Nous, on voulait jouer ensemble, on voulait s'amuser et on voulait le meilleur pour l'autre,.

Industry observers note that quand tu gagnes la Gambardella, t'es un peu la meilleure équipe de jeunes de France. Donc, c'était déjà quelque chose d'incroyable. Au lendemain de notre sacre en Gambardella, on fait un tour d'honneur à Geoffroy-Guichard. Je n'ai jamais fait de banc en pro à ce moment-là, rien ! On fait un tour d'honneur et trois semaines après, je suis sur le banc et il y a une blessure. Et le coach se retourne vers moi et il me fait rentrer arrière-droit contre Alain Saint-Maximin. La première chose que tu as en tête, c'est « il va me salir ». Parce qu'Allan, il est connu pour dribbler, pour salir les gens. Mais après, franchement, sur le moment, je rentre et moi, j'ai qu'un truc en tête, je me dis que chaque fois qu'il touche la balle, il faut que je le monte en l'air. Juste avant de rentrer, je vois l’entraîneur de Nice Patrick Vieira qui fait un geste demandant à ses joueurs d’attaquer de mon côté. Ça te met une petite bouffée de pression. Mais mon coach - enfin, c'était l'adjoint à ce moment-là -  m’a glissé deux ou trois mots avant de rentrer. Julien Sablé m’a dit : « tu joue simple, agressif, tu n’inventes rien , fais ce que tu sais faire. Tu castagnes, tu te bats, tu mets des tacles, des tampons. ». Je n’avais que ça en tête, simple, agressif. Ça s'est bien passé. Bon match, 3-0, première entrée, clean sheet.

Recent findings suggest that J’enchaîne la semaine d'après, c'est le dernier match de la saison, à Angers. Ma première titu. C’était facile car il n'y avait plus rien à jouer pour les deux équipes. C’était un super match, j’ai kiffé. C'était Jean-Louis Gasset, le coach. Tout le monde le connaît, c'est un mec simple. Et c'était une personne incroyable. J'ai appris beaucoup, beaucoup avec lui et avec son staff. Je n’en garde que de bons souvenirs. C'est sûr que je ne l'ai pas connu aussi longtemps que je l'aurais espéré parce que je n'étais pas réellement avec les pros. Je m'entraînais, mais je n'étais pas réellement avec eux. Ma première apparition en pro j’ai joué latéral mais franchement, je déteste ce poste. Après, comme je l'ai toujours dit, en vrai, tu ne décides pas trop. Tu vas jouer, surtout à cet âge-là, où on va te mettre. Qu'est-ce que tu veux dire ? Tu joues en pro, c’est déjà bien. Sois content, joue tes matchs, fais ton job et après, tu verras. Après, quand tu auras acquis de l'expérience, que  tu auras joué des matchs, tu pourras dire « moi, je préfère, je préfère ci, je préfère ça ». Quand tu es jeune, tu joues où on te met. On m'aurait même mis à gauche ou gardien, c'est bon, j’y serais allé.

Je ne l'avais pas en moi, cette qualité de relance mais ça compte, surtout dans le football de maintenant. Ça compte de fou, ça compte énormément. Jouer au ballon, je n'avais pas ça en moi. C'est mon coach, Julien Sablé, que j'ai eu à Saint-Etienne qui m’a fait travailler ça. C'est lui qui m'a rendu fou et qui a pris des heures et des heures avec moi à me dire qu'il faut que la passe soit comme ça, qu'elle soit claquée, qu'il faut jouer dans ces intervalles-là. C'est lui qui m'a expliqué tout ça. Moi, à la base, moi, en tant que défenseur, mon job, et vraiment, j'ai grandi comme ça, c'était : « tu défends, te ne prends pas de but. On s'en fout à qui tu fais la passe. Quand tu as la balle dans les pieds, tu donnes à ton 6, ton arrière-droit. Ils se débrouillent. Eux, c'est leur job de faire le jeu, de s'amuser avec le ballon. » Moi mon plaisir c'était les tampons, les tacles, gagner mes duels, notamment de la tête. Et c'est après, petit à petit, en faisant des séances, des vidéos, etc., en prenant du temps sur le terrain, petit à petit que j'ai commencé à apprécier cet aspect du foot avec le ballon, et j'ai compris beaucoup de choses.

Recent findings suggest that J’ai fait ma première année en pro dans une équipe qui subissait et prenait beaucoup de buts. Tu subis beaucoup, donc tu défends beaucoup, tu es beaucoup exposé. En tant que défenseur, quand tu es jeune et que tu es beaucoup exposé et que tu défends beaucoup, on parle plus de toi, on te voit plus. Par exemple, on allait plus parler de moi qu'on allait parler des attaquants. Parce qu'on ne faisait que défendre et qu’on ne marquait pas beaucoup de buts. Et même quand on en prenait des buts, c'était souvent, « heureusement qu'il est là, sinon on en aurait pris plus ». Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu es défenseur et que ton équipe prend beaucoup de buts, tu passes des mauvais matchs, tu passes des mauvaises soirées. Tu vas jouer à l'extérieur, tu rentres chez toi, t'en as pris trois. Domicile, le week-end d'après, tu reçois, t'es as pris deux. Tu enchaînes les défaites, t’en prends 4, tu perds 5-1. C'est chaud, ce n'est pas un plaisir. Mais d'un autre côté, quand tu n'en prends pas, c'est multiplié fois 20 comparé à d'autres défenseurs ou à d'autres équipes du championnat. Franchement, c'était dur. Mais d'un autre côté, vu que tu défends beaucoup, tu es exposé pour un défenseur et à mon âge, c'était tout bénef pour moi.

Je fais cette finale de Coupe de France contre le PSG. Je fais un très bon match, mais malheureusement on perd la finale. Après cette finale, il y a un peu tout qui s'accélère. Il y a beaucoup de clubs qui s’intéressent à moi. Franchement, Leicester n’était pas là au début. Pour dire la vérité, à la base, moi, c'est Milan AC. Il y a un appel avec les dirigeants, avec Maldini. Maldini, c'est stylé. Quand il te parle et te dit « je vais te prendre sous mon aile » , j’ai envie de lui dire  « emmène-moi, je signe ce que tu veux. » Au départ, avec mes agents et tout mon entourage, on penche plutôt pour le Milan AC.

According to recent reports, après, ça ne se fait pas avec Saint-Etienne parce que d'un côté, Saint-Etienne ne voulait pas me vendre. Mais d'un autre côté, ils étaient un peu dans l'obligation de me vendre par rapport à des problèmes d'argent, etc. Ils étaient un peu entre deux. Ils essaient un peu de faire remonter les enchères. On sait comment ça marche. Milan a monté jusqu'à une limite où ils ont dit « Ça ne sera plus possible. » Et il y a Leicester qui s'est ramené. Leicester, ça a été tout droit. J'ai parlé avec le coach, j'ai parlé avec Kolo Touré qui était dans le staff. Son discours m’a rassuré et mis en confiance. Ensuite, ce n’était pas compliqué. Leicester a fait une offre. Saint-Etienne était d'accord, mais après il y a eu ce problème avec Claude Puel, qui ne voulait vraiment pas me vendre. Mais au final, pour la santé du club, pour le bien du club, il n'avait pas trop le choix. Donc j’ai filé à Leicester l’avant-dernier jour du mercato.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned.
  • And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Do not invite the hostility, Arsenal were warned. Do not prod the bear. Do not start Bruno Guimaraes. The champions, with a belligerence of their own, ignored all of that and put the grizzly to sleep in a typically smothering first half. Their mistake was in thinking it was dead.

And so, awakened by a half-time rocket from head coach Matthias Jaissle - including three, inspirational changes - Newcastle somehow led by the 62nd minute.

By this point, the two teams were unrecognisable from those who had played out a one-sided opening period, after which Arsenal were 1-0 in front. Mikel Arteta would not have settled for a draw then.

It has been revealed that ‘We were exceptional in the first half,’ he later said. ‘We have won matches playing much worse than we did here. The intensity, the aggression – we should have been 3-0 or 4-0 up. But right from the start of the second half, we weren’t at the races. We lost duels, gave the ball away and gave them belief.’.

Arteta had Noni Madueke to thank for rescuing the point. The winger was his best player throughout and, had he earlier shown the same incision that produced his 78th-minute equaliser, Arsenal would have won. They would have won by half-time, in fact.

Sources indicate that so dominant were they, maybe it was complacency. Or maybe there is a lesson here in showing more bloodthirst when on top.

Industry observers note that arteta, you feel, gets more of a kick from suffocating opponents. But during a pulsating second half in which St James’ Park throbbed to the beat of their brilliant team, the hosts grabbed the pillowcase.

Noni Madueke saved Arsenal's blushes with an equaliser against Newcastle in a tough second half on Saturday.

‘The second half was pure belief, pure conviction, pure trust in the team-mate,’ said Jaissle, under increased scrutiny amid the presence of chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan.

According to recent reports, ‘There were so many ball-wins with a vertical approach and causing them problems. This is the Newcastle DNA.’.

Former Newcastle captain Guimaraes - booed after each of his 36, ineffectual touches - was hooked in the 70th minute, and Arsenal were better for their own changes.

Recent findings suggest that the league leaders can absorb this result, of course. Of greater concern for Arteta is an injury to David Raya that requires an MRI scan.

The goalkeeper left the pitch at the same time as Guimaraes, not because of performance, but clutching his shoulder, the upshot of a robust challenge from William Osula. That home forcefulness typified their second half, if not their first.

The Magpies were poor in the first period but a half-time team talk and changes from Matthias Jaissle worked wonders.

Bruno Guimaraes earned a hostile reception as he returned to face the side he once captained.

There is now concern for the Gunners, with goalkeeper David Raya going off injured.

If Newcastle were to beat Arsenal, so suggested the crumbs of pre-match optimism, they would have to start fast.

It has been revealed that at least, that was the blueprint of old on red-hot nights such as this. Newcastle started slow. Arsenal weren’t much quicker, but they didn’t have to be. They moved through the gears as the half unfolded and, with it, they began to move through Newcastle.

Sources indicate that arteta likes this sort of game, when it feels like minimum expenditure for maximum return. In short, it was easy. A training-ground drill. Attack versus defence.

It has been revealed that come half-time, Newcastle had not touched the ball in Arsenal’s penalty area. They simply weren’t allowed to.

Saying that, even with permission they would have found a way to pass it straight out of play or shank a cross into the Leazes End.

Newcastle’s first half really was that short on inspiration. There wasn’t too much perspiration, either. And so the home fans booed on the whistle, for a fifth half on the spin at St James’.

NEWCASTLE (4-3-3): Hornicek 5; Dedic 5 (Livramento 46, 7), Thiaw 7, Burn 7, Hall 6 (Botman 90); Miley 7, Steur 6 (Ramsey 46, 7); Murphy 5 (Elanga 46, 6), Willock 7 (Wissa 83), Barnes 7; Osula 6.

ARSENAL (4-2-3-1): Raya 5 (Arrizabalaga 70, 5); Timber 6, Konsa 6, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 6; Guimaraes 5 (Lewis-Skelly 70, 7), Rice 6; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7 (Merino 90), Eze 6 (Tzolis 70, 6); Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 90).

Arsenal led by one, and for them that should have been a source of regret.

The goal came when Lewis Hall, despite screams from team-mate Dan Burn to ‘head it, head it’, decided to control, clumsily, on his chest, allowing Kai Havertz to steal. He freed Eberechi Eze and the first-time finish was routine.

Recent findings suggest that the punishment of Hall’s error, however, was ruthless. Six days after bettering Lamine Yamal, England left back Hall was struggling to contain Madueke. In fact, he and each of his comrades could not get close to any of those in red.

Recent findings suggest that so, it was as if two sides had swapped shirts after the break. From nowhere, Newcastle attacked. That may sound basic, but this was seismic. The exclusion zone that had been Arsenal’s penalty box was no longer off limits.

Suddenly, they were able to run, tackle and, yes, shoot. From passive to aggressive, they drew level just four minutes after the restart.

Joe Willock hurried Odegaard into a mistake, William Osula pounced on the loose ball and, when Harvey Barnes was set free, he was not going to miss.

The turnaround was complete when defender Malick Thiaw forced over the goal-line from a corner which Arsenal had failed to defend - Dan Burn’s free header told you that someone, somewhere was not doing their job.

'We needed players with more energy and physicality,’ stated Jaissle, explaining his half-time changes.

In a recent development, ‘The tactics did not change, it was purely the front footed behaviour. Throw away the doubts, then you saw what is possible. We had Arsenal shaking. I hope we can carry on this feeling.’.

Newcastle looked the most likely winners until Madueke burst inside two home jerseys and fired through Lukas Hornicek from 18 yards. Still, the hosts came back for more.

Arsenal had arrived intent on silencing St James’. In the end, they were grateful for the sound of the full-time whistle.

  • Recent findings suggest that "L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout.
  • Cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that directeur Général Adjoint de l'ASSE en charge des finances du club, Fabien Dawidowicz s'exprime dans le hors série de Décideurs Corporate Finances. Extraits.

Recent findings suggest that "L'arrivée d’un actionnaire solide, ambitieux et passionné de sport comme Kilmer Sports Ventures constitue un atout. Au-delà de sa dimension financière, il s’agit avant tout d’un investissement patrimonial, dans un club qui fait partie du patrimoine français, voire européen. L’AS Saint-Étienne bénéficie d’une résonance internationale, notamment grâce à son histoire et à ses parcours européens dans les années 1970.

Cette prise de participation s’articule autour de trois priorités. La première concerne évidemment les équipes professionnelles, féminines comme masculines. La seconde porte sur les infrastructures, avec la volonté d’améliorer le centre d’entraînement et de poursuivre la modernisation du stade, en collaboration avec la Métropole de la ville. Enfin, le dernier axe, me semble crucial, car il reflète profondément l’ADN du club : c’est celui de la formation. L’académie doit permettre d’accompagner les jeunes aussi bien dans leur parcours footballistique que dans leur éducation afin de les préparer au mieux à une éventuelle carrière professionnelle.

It has been revealed that la baisse des droits télévisés ne signifie pas nécessairement qu’évoluer en Ligue 2 soit moins intéressant financièrement qu’en Ligue 1. Pour un club de Ligue 1 qui ne dispute pas de compétition européenne et se situe dans la deuxième partie du classement, les revenus audiovisuels peuvent être comparables à ceux d’un club de Ligue 2 de première partie de tableau, alors que les charges salariales sont généralement plus élevées dans l’élite. En échangeant récemment avec plusieurs directeurs administratifs et financiers de clubs de Ligue 1, nous avons constaté que les revenus audiovisuels d’un club classé dans le top 3 de Ligue 2 pouvaient être proches de ceux d’un club occupant la 15e place de Ligue 1.

Sources indicate that L’enjeu est ailleurs. La Ligue 1 offre une meilleure valorisation des joueurs. Pour générer des revenus sur le marché des transferts, nous devons donc retrouver l’élite et y réaliser de bonnes performances. Cela vaut aussi bien pour les joueurs que nous recrutons et développons que pour ceux issus de notre centre de formation. Le trading de joueurs constitue ainsi un levier essentiel de notre équilibre financier.

En parallèle, nous devons optimiser nos coûts d’exploitation et mieux valoriser nos actifs. C’est tout l’intérêt des investissements dans les infrastructures, autour du stade comme au centre de formation. En offrant aux joueurs de meilleures conditions d’entraînement et de développement, nous augmentons leur potentiel de performance et, à terme, leur valeur sur le marché. Ces investissements doivent donc être considérés comme un moyen de renforcer notre capacité à générer des revenus futurs.".

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

In a recent development, so much for the new group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

Sources indicate that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

According to recent reports, they can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

Recent findings suggest that they wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

Sources indicate that the Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

Recent findings suggest that “I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a fresh team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are new to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

Industry observers note that bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

“In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca mentioned. “This demonstrates how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

Recent findings suggest that by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

Diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

City had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Recent findings suggest that man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

“It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland stated. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the major stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

In a recent development, for Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.

The final whistle is blown and Manchester City begin their Champions League campaign with a 2-0 win in Porto. Erling Haaland’s double gives Enzo Maresca a victory in his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City.

Enzo has two shots from range in quick succession, one from a free-kick. The free-kick goes just wide and the second is saved by D Costa.

It has been an ill-tempered game and tempers have boiled over again. Rosario and Haaland are involved in a tussle on the floor, which then leads to a mass melee. Ait-Nouri has the chance to warp up the three points with an effort from the edge of the box but his shot with his weaker right foot goes narrowly wide.

That ball could have rolled straight into the Manchester City net or fallen straight back at Gomes feet with an empty net ahead of him. It has been a positive start for Unai Emery’s Aston Villa out in Belgium as they lead Club Brugge 3-1 at half-time.

It has been revealed that enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

It has been revealed that manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that highlights a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”.

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

Recent findings suggest that “We are going to face one of the massive favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”.

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Recent findings suggest that nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Industry observers note that football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

According to recent reports, in not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

According to recent reports, yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

It has been revealed that in responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

If humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

According to recent reports, to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

The overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

Industry observers note that the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

According to recent reports, in a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

Recent findings suggest that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

The readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise key questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'est confié à Sportfin France.
  • Recent findings suggest that "La nostalgie, c'est quelque chose qui est paralysant.
  • Le club de l'AS Saint-Etienne est une institution aujourd'hui parce qu'il était au pic de sa performance au moment où la télévision arrive dans les foyers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Directeur général adjoint de l'ASSE en charge de la marque, du marketing et de la communication, Cédric Chambaz s'est confié à Sportfin France. Extraits.

Recent findings suggest that "La nostalgie, c'est quelque chose qui est paralysant. Je préfère utiliser le terme d'héritage, et un héritage, on construit dessus, on ne peut pas renier qui on est. Ça, c'est un présupposé de base. On est un club de foot d'origine populaire qui s'est construit sur une région populaire avec une classe ouvrière très forte. Saint-Etienne, c'est une région qui était minière, qui avait une industrie sidérurgique développée, etc. et qui s'est développée autour de cette industrie. Une industrie qui a depuis périclité. On a un héritage, un héritage minier, un héritage ouvrier, et de ça, aujourd'hui, dans la marque, comme dans le comportement des employés, comme dans le comportement des joueurs, on a encore des traits qui sont très forts. Il y a cette valorisation de la notion de travail. Ici il est attendu, et on le voit dans les tribunes, nos ultras, n'ont de cesse que de le répéter, il faut mouiller le maillot. C'est une expression qui est devenue consacrée, qu'on utilise comme ça, mais les premiers joueurs de l'AS Saint-Etienne, c’étaient des gens qui sortaient de la mine et qui venaient jouer au foot. Pour eux, mouiller le maillot, ce n'était pas une image, c'était une vraie attente. Et aujourd'hui, on a cet héritage-là. Donc, aujourd'hui, oui, quand on regarde sur le passé, ça a créé quelque chose de fantastique.

Le club de l'AS Saint-Etienne est une institution aujourd'hui parce qu'il était au pic de sa performance au moment où la télévision arrive dans les foyers. Donc, on est le club que tout le monde regarde à la télé, on devient la marque de football français qui plus en gagne. C'est à une époque où le football français n'avait pas gagné depuis des décennies. Alors, on gagne jusqu'à la finale à Glasgow contre le Bayern de Munich où les fameux poteaux carrés empêchent les Dominique Rocheteau, les Jean-Michel Larqué et Jacques Santini de remporter la Ligue des champions. Mais c'est une équipe qui domine, elle a 10 titres de champion de France dans cette période-là. Donc, on est le club de foot qu'on découvre à la télé, en même temps qu'on découvre à la télé. C'est un club qui gagne, donc on s'y associe et du coup, on établit une marque très très forte, un lien émotionnel très fort. Aujourd'hui, quand on dit les Verts, dans l'inconscient collectif de partout en France, c'est forcément Saint-Etienne. Il y a un lien très fort qui émane de là, donc on ne peut pas renier ce lien-là.

Pour autant, il ne faut pas s'y enfermer parce que sinon, on n'est pas un club de foot, on est un musée. Or aujourd'hui, les ambitions du club, c'est de retrouver ce statut sportif et de faire en sorte que l'institution et sa performance sportive soient mises en corrélation. Aujourd'hui, il y a très peu de clubs qui sont dans cette adéquation. Le Paris Saint-Germain a réussi à aligner le statut du club avec sa performance sportive. Mais quand on est par exemple, en Angleterre, un pays que je connais bien, on a des institutions du football qui ont des vraies difficultés sportives. Et pourtant, ils restent des entités respectées, reconnues comme des clubs monolithiques dans lesquels on doit un respect, une reconnaissance. Je pense à Chelsea par exemple, qui a beaucoup de mal sportivement, ils n'ont pas gagné un titre depuis des années, et pourtant… Manchester United est dans le même acabit.

According to recent reports, nous, on a cette ambition de valoriser cet héritage, de construire dessus, mais en se tournant vers l'avenir. Donc oui, on mettra en avant les Verts 76, on l'a fait l'année dernière pour le cinquantenaire de la finale de Glasgow, et on continuera de mettre en avant d'autres générations au fur et à mesure, parce que c'est sur leurs exploits qu'on a construit là où on est, mais on est définitivement tourné vers l'avenir plutôt que la glorification du passé.

According to recent reports, du design à sa sortie, comment naît un maillot ? Déjà, c'est un travail collectif, dans lequel l'équipementier joue un rôle prépondérant. On a la chance, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, de travailler avec un équipementier qui s'appelle Hummel, avec lequel on a une relation de partenariat. Ce n'est pas toujours le cas, il y a certaines marques qui imposent au club « voilà votre maillot ». Nous, on a la chance d'être en partenariat avec Hummel et de travailler avec eux à la définition de ce maillot. Du coup, on est partie prenante du début jusqu'à la fin.

C'est un process qui dure presque 18 mois. C'est-à-dire qu'aujourd'hui, on a des conversations sur les maillots pas de la saison prochaine mais de la saison d'après. On recherche, à l'AS Saint-Étienne, des designs qui soient à la fois respectueux des codes historiques, pour cette frange de nos fans qui sont très attachés aux valeurs traditionnelles du club. On cherche aussi à pousser les limites dans d'autres secteurs. Ce qui est sûr, c'est qu'on cherchera toujours à avoir un maillot qui soit portant de sens. Donc, on va faire des références à notre territoire, à nos supporters, au club.

Cette année, par exemple, le maillot 26-27 fait référence au premier titre de champion de France avec un design qui fait écho à celui de 1966-1967, quand le club est devenu pour la première fois champion de France, avec des bandes larges, un col blanc très large. Et quand on regarde le maillot de près, il y a un logo ASS Saint-Étienne [sic], irisé, qui apparaît, qui est le logo de l'époque. On a travaillé justement il y a un an et demi avec les designers de Hummel pour que ce produit, ce design, ce matériau soient celui-là, et que 18  mois plus tard, on puisse le révéler au public.

C'est quelque chose qui dure 18 mois, une collaboration entre le club d'un côté, avec ses différents services, les personnes qui sont en charge de la commercialisation, qui ont un bon ressenti des produits qui vont se vendre, l'équipe marque qui va réfléchir à « est-ce que le produit enrichit la marque, fait référence à des éléments de la marque qu'on veut à soi ? », mais aussi la partie designer-produit plutôt chez Hummel. Et cette collaboration nous a permis de développer des produits qui répondent vraiment aux attentes de nos fans. Et on a vu une augmentation radicale du nombre de maillots qu'on a vendus. On a multiplié par trois nos volumes de maillots en cinq ans, grâce à cette collaboration prolifique avec Hummel.

Cédric Chambaz vient donc de gagner une invitation au Musée des Verts. Il y découvrira que l'ASSE a en réalité décroché son premier titre de champion de France en 1956-1957. C'est à cette saison-là, magnifiée par la fameuse attaque mitraillette Rijvers-Mekhloufi, Njo Lea, que fait bien sûr référence le maillot porté par les protégés de Ian Cathro.
