The Netherlands came crashing down to earth after hammering Greece as they were outclassed and outmuscled by Germany in Berlin.

Oranje went into the final match of the Nations League group stage with high hopes of recording their first win over their old rivals in seven matches stretching back to 2019.

Instead they suffered their second worst defeat ever at the hands of Germany, but still progressed to the knockout stages thanks to their thumping 7-0 win in Amsterdam on Friday.

Coach Xavi Hernandez was forced to make one change in midfield as Jurriën Timber replaced Barcelona’s Frenkie de Jong, who pulled out with an obturator muscle strain.

Germany shaded the first half and went ahead five minutes before the break when Freiburg striker Derry Scherhant cut in from the left hand side and beat Bart Verbruggen with a curling strike into the top corner.

Scherhant had struck the post minutes earlier, while the Dutch might have taken the lead earlier when Crysencio Summerville slipped in the penalty area as he tried to control a cross by Cody Gakpo.

In a recent development, but in the second half the Dutch fell apart. In the 60th minute Florian Wirtz shoved Denzel Dumfries off the ball and had space to tee up a left-footed shot from the edge of the area that gave Verbruggen no chance.

Nico Schlotterbeck added a third from a free-kick five minutes later, before Wirtz drifted past Gakpo on the right side of the penalty area to score his second.

The humiliation was complete when Brajan Gruda capped a fine attacking performance by firing in a rebound.

Recent findings suggest that dumfries made no excuses afterwards for what he admitted was a “terrible performance”. “We gave the ball away too easily, left too much space and were too weak in the challenges,” he told NOS. “We can’t let that happen.”.

KILMARNOCK 2 ABERDEEN 4: Dazzling Dons get a Frick pick-up but it's more misery for McCann's men

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (967 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.
  • In Mario Frick, they may have got their man.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:33 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:15 EST, 21 November 2026.

Having been bored senseless by the football offered up under Stephen Robinson, Aberdeen supporters were – at the very least – crying out for the next appointment to provide some sort of entertainment to get excited about over the dark winter months.

In Mario Frick, they may have got their man. Whether or not the former Luzern boss will be a success at Pittodrie is anyone’s guess. But on this evidence, it’s going to be a lot of fun watching him have a go.

At times, they were scintillating here on their way to a thrilling win which moved them five clear of their hosts and provided some much-needed breathing room ahead of a tricky upcoming schedule which involves trips to Ibrox and Tynecastle, as well as two home clashes against the Dundee clubs.

Yes, it wasn’t perfect. Far from it, in fact. Defensively, they were far too open. Kilmarnock just weren’t good enough to take full advantage.

But you suspect that will be forgiven to an extent as long as they can play with this level of panache and aggression going forward.

Findlay Marshall celebrates after scoring the Dons' fourth goal at Rugby Park.

Industry observers note that frick has arrived with the promise of bringing ‘heavy metal’ football to Pittodrie. It’s taken a little over 90 minutes to understand what he's talking about.

According to recent reports, ‘It was very chaotic,’ he admitted. ‘It's quite different to Switzerland, because there is technicality, but it’s not as physical as it was today.

‘It was difficult. We were lucky as well because Killie, especially in the second half, played very well, but I think at the end it's a deserved victory.

‘When the players were young, they didn’t think about mistakes, didn’t think about any negatives.

‘They played only to win for fun, and I told them to play as if they were young players and I think, especially first half, it was very good.

‘You don't know what's going on or what can happen in this first game, so I'm very happy we won.’.

Frick reveals his delight after tasting victory in his first match in charge of Aberdeen.

Kilmarnock spurned a golden opportunity to take a sixth-minute lead at the end of a rapid counter-attack, with Joe Hugill finding himself all alone in the Dons box.

Industry observers note that the striker took a heavy first touch, allowing Marius Muller to promptly narrow the angle and block the effort. It’s easy to see why Hugill has found the back of the net just twice this year.

And the hosts were made to pay for that miss within 90 seconds as Aberdeen went in front.

In a recent development, for the umpteenth time this season, Killie failed to clear their lines under little pressure, with Stuart Armstrong teeing up Kevin Nisbet to sweep home a lovely finish from the edge of the area. The unsighted Nico Mantl in the Killie goal didn’t even move.

Mind you, he should have done significantly better four minutes later as Nisbet notched his second of the afternoon.

The keeper’s positioning as the Dons striker stepped up to send a low free-kick in off the post was as poor as it gets.

You got the feeling that the walls would have caved in had Aberdeen grabbed a third, but a brief drop-off in intensity from Frick’s side enabled Killie to drag themselves back into the contest.

A bit of pinball outside the Dons box saw the ball fall favourably for skipper Greg Kiltie 12 yards out, who adjusted his body brilliantly to drill beyond Muller on the half-volley.

Yet with a defence as dodgy as this, manager Neil McCann can never feel overly confident.

Ante Palaversa – terrific on his first appearance of the season – was given far too much time in the centre circle to get his head up and pick out Nesta Guinness-Walker on the left.

He glided past MJ Kamson-Kamara as if he wasn’t there before dinking a ball right on to the head of Brad Lyons, who rose completely unopposed to power home against his former employers.

If Killie continue to defend like this, relegation is a certainty. Will the manager even get the chance to turn it around? Going off the abuse being hurled in his direction from the home punters, his jacket is evidently on a shoogly peg. Many fans have already made up their mind.

Nisbet's free-kick finds the net for his second as the Dons take control of the game.

In a recent development, michael Schjonning-Larsen’s deflected effort from 20 yards shortly after the restart looked destined for the goal before Muller instinctively leapt to his right to claw it away on the line. It was a superb stop.

His next contribution defied belief.

Goodness knows what the keeper was thinking as he tried to pass out from the six-yard line, playing it straight to the feet of Tyreece John-Jules – only just on the park – who steadied himself before finishing.

You would have stuck your house on Nisbet putting this one to bed with five minutes remaining, however with just Mantl to beat, he pulled his left-footed effort wide.

Findlay Marshall indicated him how it’s done with stoppage-time looming, running half the length of the field before drilling low into the corner to consign Killie to another sobering defeat.

McCann said: ‘I probably sound like a broken record, but we create really big, big chances, and we don't take them.

According to recent reports, ‘We're letting games pass us by. We're giving teams the opportunity to start ahead of us because of the goals we're conceding and then it's difficult to work back.’.

Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.
  • On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness.
  • And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a latest contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face remarked it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W.

In a recent development, there are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he highlighted during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

It has been revealed that for Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Industry observers note that liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo indicated he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

Sources indicate that there was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

According to recent reports, llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc.

Industry observers note that we knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

It has been revealed that atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

Industry observers note that the question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

Sources indicate that “I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”.

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE.

Kerkez is right now down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

According to recent reports, atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The substantial challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The upcoming Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

Sources indicate that the Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed upcoming contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:.

Industry observers note that “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a newly introduced contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

Sources indicate that “I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”.

Recent findings suggest that former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

It has been revealed that the Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what significant clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”.

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

Recent findings suggest that “I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

Recent findings suggest that “It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a substantial responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”.

Sources indicate that atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

Recent findings suggest that “We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone remarked. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”.

Ajax moved into a clear second place in the Eredivisie with a routine 3-0 win against ADO Den Haag, as Feyenood slipped to fifth after losing to local rivals Excelsior.

Davy Klaassen took just three minutes to stroke home the opening goal for Ajax and added a second just before half-time.

By then ADO had been reduced to 10 men following the dismissal of Matteo Waem for hauling down Tolu Arakodare.

But there was a blow for Ajax ahead of next weekend’s visit to Feyenoord when Jorthy Mokio, scorer of the second goal, was taken off injured after an accidental collision with Sékou Sylla.

Feyenoord, who started the month top of the Eredivisie, suffered their first home defeat in the derby against Excelsior since 1980 to continue a slump in form that has seen them draw two and lose four of their last six games.

Sources indicate that givairo Read’s blistering shot gave Feyenoord the lead after just two minutes, but Excelsior were ahead by half-time and made it 3-1 when Casper Windell headed in a corner after 58 minutes. Despite an own goal by Jan Plug, on loan from Feyenoord, Excelsior were not to be denied.

PSV remain a point clear of Ajax at the top of the table after they cruised to a 4-1 win at NEC, with Filip Kostic opening the scoring with his first goal for PSV and his first Eredivisie goal since 2014, when he was playing for Groningen.

Utrecht sacked their managed Anthony Correia after just 14 matches after sinking to 15th place in the table with a 3-2 home defeat to Cambuur.

It has been revealed that correia won just four games after leaving Telstar, the club he led to promotion two seasons ago and where he spent his entire 15-year playing career. Youth team coach Mark Otten will take charge of the first team while Utrecht search for a replacement.

Willem II, searching for their first Eredivisie win in 30 matches, took a shock lead away to Twente despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half when Devin Haen was given space in the area to shoot past Joël Drommel.

The home side struggled to turn their superiority into goals, but an equaliser by Ramiz Zerrouki and a late header by Marko Pjaca gave them the points they needed to rise to third place above Feyenoord.

AZ also overtook Feyenoord as they beat Sparta 5-1 with a dominant second-half display, while Fortuna Sittard kept in touch with the leading group with a typically gritty 1-0 win at Go Ahead Eagles.

Go Ahead Eagles 0-1 Fortuna Sittard.

New system, same problems: Thomas Frank's first game in charge of Crystal Palace ends in defeat despite tactical switch... but Coventry are up to 13th

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.
  • Sources indicate that there were, however, some noticeable improvements.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:02 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 16:52 EST, 21 November 2026.

Thomas Frank might have changed formation in his first game in charge of Crystal Palace, but there was no change in fortune for the Premier League’s bottom club.

Sources indicate that there were, however, some noticeable improvements. Palace were more structured in attack, with cleverly orchestrated moves and a clear, coherent initiative for creating chances.

According to recent reports, but the same problem that plagued his predecessor Pierre Sage persisted: Palace cannot defend. That diagnosis is simple to make. However, addressing it is complicated by inadequate personnel.

Palace replaced Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix with teenage defender Honest Ahanor and Chelsea castoff Axel Disasi in the summer.

Until they can address the oversight in their squad planning - thinking that would be enough to replace two international centre-backs - they will continue to ship sloppy goals.

Frank will be able to address the structural problems, ensure players understand the positions they should occupy in specific situations and get Palace defending as a cohesive unit.

These are all things within his control and he began fixing them to some extent on Saturday.

Despite having a upcoming manager in the dugout, the same old problems remained for Crystal Palace.

His in-game management worked to a degree as Palace conceded two goals and defended frantically in the first half before looking much more solid and organised in the second period before finally conceding the decisive goal in the 85th minute.

What he won’t be able to eradicate, though, are the individual errors that have consistently cost Palace this season.

Ultimately, those mistakes come down to the quality of the defenders at his disposal.

Palace will look to address their personnel concerns in January but they right now sit rock bottom of the league, with a massive game against Hull next Sunday.

Unless they can cut out the errors that have contributed to their 27 league goals conceded this season, they risk being cut adrift before they can bring in reinforcements.

Upcoming boss Frank was more glass-half-full, though. ‘There is more positive than negative from the game,’ Frank said. ‘We looked like a threat. We scored two very good goals and we created quite a few more chances to score at least one more goal.

It has been revealed that ‘That was the massive positive. I was extremely happy with the effort and the mentality of the players.’.

Defensively, this was a horror show. Three players were dragged out wide — including Disasi, who was miles out of position — allowing Jack Rudoni to find Taiwo Awoniyi in the penalty area to poke past Dean Henderson four minutes into Frank’s first assignment.

Coventry should have had a second, too, after Palace overcommitted in attack and Awoniyi was played in behind. One-on-one with Dean Henderson, he took the ball around the goalkeeper, only for Axel Disasi to somehow get back and clear it off the line.

Palace had been on the front foot but were caught out by how quickly they had to transition from attack to defence, unable to get enough bodies back in time. They are struggling to find a balance between defence and attack.

Dwight McNeil's own goal cost Palace late on as they slumped to a 3-2 defeat.

It has been revealed that anan Khalaili failed to win his tackle for Coventry’s second, giving Rudoni space to run down the right. Nobody shut Rudoni down and he found Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, who rocketed a thunderous half-volley into the top corner from outside the area.

Coventry’s 85th-minute winner came from a long throw, which Palace failed to deal with.

Frank abandoned the back three, which had served Palace well for the last two years and nine months, and pivoted to a 4-2-3-1.

Recent findings suggest that offensively, Palace improved. The formation suited Yeremy Pino and Jorgen Strand Larsen particularly well, with the pair combining for both of Palace’s goals.

It should also bring the best out of Quinten Timber, Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton, as individuals are rarely isolated in midfield, unlike under Pierre Sage.

On the other hand, Tyrick Mitchell and Khalaili still tried to function as wing-backs rather than full-backs.

In a recent development, that is ingrained in their habits, and it will take time to coach it out of them. However, it remains a significant issue.

Both players committed themselves forward when attacking, leaving an already fragile centre-back pairing exposed and allowing Coventry to transition quickly and exploit Palace's vulnerability.

That cannot happen in a back four, as there were situations where Palace had eight players forward with only the goalkeeper and two centre-backs staying back.

Coventry were far from convincing defensively but found a way to beat their relegation rivals, climbing to 13th on 12 points, three clear of the drop zone.

Tatsuhiro Sakamoto celebrates scoring Coventry's second with Jack Rudoni.

Frank Lampard’s side have now won four of their last seven games and sit above fellow promoted sides Hull and Ipswich — an impressive feat after losing their first four games back in the Premier League.

Industry observers note that the Coventry boss remarked: ‘It’s a big win for us. Every win for us in this league is a big win. But when a game is that tight, it’s key to get what we got.

‘After our start, where we played the best three teams in the league, we had zero points after four games, and now where we are is great progression.

‘That’s only down to hard work. We are the underdog in most games, so for them to experience and live difficult moments that this league will bring, it will help the players grow.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Les sites FLASHSCORE et SOFASCORE ont figé leurs statistiques à l'issue de la rencontre remportée par les Verts à Reims (1-0), pour le compte de la 13me journée de Ligue 2.

According to recent reports, sur les vingt données extraites des deux plateformes sportives, les deux équipes ne sont pas parvenues à se départager : dix statistiques sont en faveur des Verts, les dix autres, fatalement, pour le Stade de Reims. Match nul donc.

Sources indicate that dans le jeu avec et sans ballon, les Stéphanois ont perdu le match de la possession (46% vs 54%), tout comme ils l'avaient perdu contre Montpellier (45% vs 55%), à Metz (46% vs 54%), au Red Star (41% vs 59%) et à Sochaux (47% vs 53%). Cinq défaites en ce qui concerne le monopole du ballon mais quatre victoires et un nul au coup de sifflet final (quatre prétendants à la montée rencontrés). Cependant, les Verts ont devancé leur adversaire du soir dans les duels relatifs à la distance kilométrique parcourue (104,3 km vs 98,3 km) et aux sprints à haute intensité (121 vs 115).

Pour ce qui est des passes, les Champenois sont devant partout : les passes réussies (87% vs 83%), les passes longues réussies (52% vs 33%) ainsi que les passes réussies dans le dernier tiers (74% vs 64%). Après Sochaux, Montpellier, Metz et le Red Star, c'est donc la cinquième fois de la saison que les Stéphanois ne dominent pas leur sujet dans ce domaine, en étant même en dessous de leur moyenne constatée avant cette 13ème journée. Cinq défaites dans le match des passes cette fois-ci, pour quatre victoires et un nul à la fin du temps réglementaire.

Sur le plan offensif, Sainté domine Reims sur cinq des huit métriques remontées avec notamment un xG de 1,45 (vs 0,97), un xGOT de 1,06 (vs 0.16), 21 ballons touchés dans la surface adverse contre 20, 2 occasions à 1 et un pourcentage de précision dans les tirs deux fois plus élevé (43% vs 21%).

Dans le secteur défensif, en revanche, les Verts ont perdu la bataille des duels (46% des duels joués, 44 sur 95) et des tacles réussis (64% vs 75%).

Industry observers note that par ailleurs, les Verts se sont vu attribuer par FLASHSCORE la note globale de 6.9 vs 6.6 pour Reims. Au niveau individuel, c'est Z.Davitashvili qui est élu "homme du match" avec une note de 7.9 (pour 32 minutes de temps passé sur le terrain de jeu) devant A.Boakye (7.6), D.Guindo, le latéral rémois (7.4), I.Cardona (7.3), M.Ndiaye (7.2) à égalité avec deux autres Champenois, S.Kotto et T.Leoni. Enfin, trois autres Stéphanois ont obtenu la note de 7.0 : A.Csongvai, K.Pedro et J.Le Cardinal.

I.Cathro a notamment déclaré : "C'est une victoire très importante. On a été intelligents. L'équipe a appris au fil du match, a été équilibrée. On savait que cet adversaire avait de la qualité et qu'on devait lui donner peu d'opportunités pour s'exprimer". Une victoire très importante effectivement qui permet à Sainté de creuser momentanément un écart conséquent sur Reims : +10 points au soir du 13ème acte de cette Ligue 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L'Assessore ai Grandi Eventi, Sport, Turismo e Moda, Alessandro Onorato, è intervenuto ai microfoni di Radio Laziale, in cui ha parlato degli ultimi aggiornamenti sullo stadio Flaminio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that stadio Flaminio? In molti pensavano che la proposta della Lazio non fosse reale, invece il progetto esiste. Si è conclusa la Conferenza dei Servizi, che ha espresso parere favorevole, pur prevedendo una serie di prescrizioni e osservazioni. Tra agosto e settembre la Lazio ha presentato alcune proposte di modifica alla Soprintendenza statale, della quale attendiamo le risposte. Qualora venisse confermata l’accettazione delle modifiche, che prevedono una riduzione di pochi metri dell’altezza, il club dovrà rielaborare il piano economico-finanziario. A quel punto il Comune potrà esprimersi sul riconoscimento o meno dell’interesse pubblico. Si ipotizza una riduzione della capienza di 4-5mila posti, arrivando a un totale di circa 45mila spettatori. Sulla sostenibilità economica potremo esprimere un giudizio definitivo soltanto quando riceveremo il piano aggiornato sulla base delle varianti. Un progetto approvato dal Comune deve necessariamente garantire un equilibrio finanziario, mentre l’individuazione di chi finanzierà l’opera rappresenta un passaggio successivo. Attualmente è la Lazio ad attendere la risposta della Soprintendenza statale. Una volta ricevuta, sarà il Comune ad aspettare che la società aggiorni il piano economico-finanziario. Con il sindaco Gualtieri ci auguriamo di concludere questo percorso quanto prima, perché, al di là di Lotito e delle simpatie personali, l’obiettivo è evitare che il Flaminio rimanga in queste imbarazzanti condizioni di degrado. Abbiamo lavorato a lungo su questo impianto, anche perché in passato erano stati presentati altri progetti. In questo caso si tratterebbe di un investimento interamente a carico della Lazio.

Recent findings suggest that il rapporto con Lotito? Riesco a distinguere il mio ruolo di assessore da quello di tifoso. Come assessore mantengo un atteggiamento imparziale: non contano le simpatie personali, ma i fatti. Il progetto del Flaminio è estremamente complesso, in tanti ci hanno provato senza mai riuscirci. Comprendo anche le preoccupazioni dei residenti, ma già oggi quella zona è difficilmente vivibile. Le normative attuali per autorizzare la riqualificazione del Flaminio sono profondamente diverse rispetto al passato: bisogna dimostrare scientificamente la gestione dei flussi di ingresso e uscita degli spettatori, la sicurezza dell’intera area e molto altro. Per questo sono convinto che, qualora si arrivasse alla conclusione del percorso, ci sarebbe un miglioramento oggettivo per il quartiere rispetto alla situazione attuale durante le partite all’Olimpico.

Industry observers note that L’intervista al Foglio su Lotito? Tutto nasce dalla richiesta di un giornalista di commentare le minacce di morte rivolte a Lotito, alle quali ho risposto sottolineando la gravità della vicenda. Il giorno successivo è uscito il titolo “Onorato difende Lotito”, quando nel resto dell’intervista avevo affrontato molte altre questioni. Da tifoso ritengo evidente che Lotito abbia commesso gravi errori nella comunicazione e nel coinvolgimento della tifoseria, e l’ho ribadito più volte. Se poi si vuole far passare il messaggio che io sia contrario alla protesta soltanto perché sono andato una volta allo stadio per evitare che i miei figli di 6 e 10 anni perdessero l’amore per i colori biancazzurri, credo sia un tentativo becero di alimentare ulteriormente le divisioni. Un’altra cosa che mi infastidisce molto è la volontà di distinguere i tifosi della Lazio in categorie di Serie A, B e C. È assurdo: la tifoseria è una sola, non esistono tifosi più puri di altri.

According to recent reports, posso garantire che ogni volta che incontro Lotito gli ribadisco la necessità di assumere atteggiamenti di maggiore distensione e apertura nei confronti della tifoseria. Diffidate dei politici che sfruttano le proteste per ottenere qualche voto in più, perché trovo molto strano questo comportamento. Per me l’amore verso una squadra è qualcosa di sacro, perché senza tifosi il calcio non esiste. Allo stesso tempo, considero surreale che qualcuno possa decidere per gli altri quali comportamenti adottare. Ho visto circolare alcuni video nei quali sembrerebbe che io abbia sostenuto la scelta di Lotito di togliere il merchandising agli Irriducibili. In realtà il mio ragionamento era diverso: vogliamo che le società italiane raggiungano il livello di quelle inglesi, spagnole, tedesche e francesi? Allora servono stadi di proprietà e il merchandising rappresenta una delle principali fonti di ricavo. Riuscite a immaginare un emiro che acquista la Lazio e al quale viene detto che il merchandising è gestito dai tifosi? È un ragionamento poco realistico. Lo dice una persona che da ragazzo frequentava la curva e che ha acquistato liberamente le sciarpe degli Irriducibili e degli altri gruppi organizzati. Ma quello è un altro discorso. Dobbiamo alzare il livello del confronto.

L’altro ieri abbiamo assistito ancora una volta a scontri tra i tifosi del Torino e della Roma. Per quanto tempo dovremo continuare a vedere episodi di violenza legati al calcio? Chi può essere interessato a investire in questo settore se non riusciamo a renderlo sicuro, permettendo ai tifosi di vivere naturalmente la propria passione? Io andavo allo stadio con il club Re Cecconi di Ostia, partendo da piazza Quarto dei Mille con il pullman organizzato e il panino con la frittata. Sono profondamente legato al calcio romantico, ma se in una piazza come Roma vogliamo tornare a sognare, anche noi tifosi dobbiamo avere un approccio diverso. Perché tanti attori e cantanti laziali non dichiarano apertamente la propria fede calcistica? Quanti politici romani lo fanno? Io, Alessandro Cochi e pochi altri. Perché accade questo? Perché tutto diventa complicato, tutto si trasforma in polemica. Dobbiamo superare queste divisioni: siamo un’unica tifoseria, un unico popolo. Nutro il massimo rispetto per chi oggi protesta, perché rappresenta un grande sacrificio e lo comprendo.

Una data per il Flaminio? Se fossi un radioascoltatore e sentissi un assessore indicare una data, impazzirei. Quello che posso garantire, assumendomi la responsabilità del mio ruolo, è che il progetto è concreto e che siamo agli ultimi passaggi prima dell’eventuale approvazione da parte del Comune. Successivamente l’iter prevede un avviso pubblico, con un ulteriore anno di procedure. Se poi Lotito deciderà effettivamente di realizzarlo oppure no, non posso saperlo: bisogna prima arrivare a quel momento. Ma, una volta ottenute tutte le autorizzazioni, possiamo riconoscere che avere lo stadio Flaminio nel cuore della città rappresenterebbe una grande opportunità di crescita per la Lazio? Credo proprio di sì. Oggi incontro tifosi che mi abbracciano e mi chiedono di non far realizzare lo stadio, mentre fino a due anni fa mi chiedevano esattamente il contrario. Il mio invito è semplicemente quello di mantenere la calma.

Comprendo la rabbia, ma ricoprendo il ruolo di assessore del Comune di Roma non ho la libertà di esprimermi come un semplice tifoso. Quando si rappresenta un’istituzione bisogna rispettare i propri doveri istituzionali. Lo stadio della Roma rappresenta una grande opportunità per la città, e lo affermo nonostante sia facilmente immaginabile quale sarà il mio stato d’animo quando andrò al derby. È un progetto importante perché consentirà di riqualificare un’area, porterà un investimento significativo e creerà numerosi posti di lavoro. Quando alcuni tifosi della Lazio mi criticano per le vicende legate a Lotito, ne soffro. Non certamente per una questione elettorale: se avessi voluto ottenere consensi in maniera opportunistica, non avrei mai dichiarato nulla, considerando che a Roma ci sono più romanisti. Ma non è questo che mi interessa. Sono diventato laziale in prima elementare proprio perché nessuno tifava Lazio e sono abituato alle critiche. Essere laziali significa anche saper essere soli, è uno stile di vita. Ciò che mi dispiace maggiormente è vedere un laziale attaccare un altro laziale. È qualcosa che mi fa soffrire. Non riscontro lo stesso atteggiamento nella tifoseria romanista, che a volte arriva persino a negare l’evidenza pur di mantenere il senso di comunità. Stiamo attraversando un momento drammatico nei rapporti tra tifoseria e presidenza, ne sono consapevole. Ma cerchiamo di mantenere la calma.

Latest Update: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

📅 09 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5333 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the upcoming Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.
  • Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the upcoming Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4.

Sources indicate that in five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” stated Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”.

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

According to recent reports, “With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” noted Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”.

In a recent development, there was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r.

Recent findings suggest that A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

In a recent development, even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Sources indicate that despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

According to recent reports, “It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.

The absence of Scott McTominay due to a minor heart problem is good news for Arsenal, who are likely to make a few changes to the team that beat Chelsea so impressively at the weekend.

Welcome back to another night of Champions League football direct to your mobile/desktop/electronic device of your choosing!

Both Aston Villa and Manchester City got off to winning starts last night, beating Club Brugge and Porto respectively. Other fun fixtures included Real Madrid beating Inter Milan, getting Jose Mourinho his own winning return in Europe with Madrid. Now it’s Arsenal’s turn.

After falling at the final hurdle last season – losing on penalties to Paris St-Germain in Budapest – they have travelled to the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples, hoping to take the first step of a fresh attempt to claim their white whale.

According to recent reports, their Italian hosts have not had the smoothest start to the 2026-27 campaign, settling under new manager Massimiliano Allegri. While Antonio Conte guided them to a second-place finish in Serie A last season, they have only managed one win from three league games – losing to Como and Inter Milan – meaning that they presently sit 12th in the league.

They were eliminated after the league phase of the Champions League last year, finishing to 30th out of 36 teams, and will surely be looking to improve on that poor performance this season.

As for the Premier Champions, who have started their domestic season with a 100 per cent record, they will have their eyes on the prize from the get-go. They were formidable in the league phase last year, winning all eight matches and scoring 23 goals while conceding just four.

We will be getting team news shortly and will be bringing you the pre-match updates as they come.

Despite the carnage at UK airports this week, Sam Dean has made it to Naples and will be bringing us updates from the continent.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ayant marqué 3 buts cette saison en championnat des U17 nationaux (contre Villefranche-sur-Saône, Ajaccio et Saint-Priest), l'attaquant stéphanois Izaya Kimpioka fait partie des 34 joueurs sélectionnés en équipe de France U16 pour un stage de 5 jours à Clairefontaine lors duquel il affrontera les U17 du Paris FC (le mercredi 2 décembre à 15h00) et les U17 du VAFC (le jeudi 3 décembre à 11h00).

Ayant marqué 3 buts cette saison en championnat des U17 nationaux (contre Villefranche-sur-Saône, Ajaccio et Saint-Priest), l'attaquant stéphanois Izaya Kimpioka fait partie des 34 joueurs sélectionnés en équipe de France U16 pour un stage de 5 jours à Clairefontaine lors duquel il affrontera les U17 du Paris FC (le mercredi 2 décembre à 15h00) et les U17 du VAFC (le jeudi 3 décembre à 11h00).

Il ya quelques mois, du 28 au 31 mai 2026, Izaya Kimpioka avait déjà été convoqué, tout comme Adam Charreyre, à un stage à Clairefontaine, en compagnie des 72 meilleurs jeunes de la génération 2011.Izaya Kimpioka a débuté le football à Sainte-Geneviève en U6 avant de rejoindre Brétigny en U7. Il est ensuite passé au FC Fleury en U11 et a intègré l’INF Clairefontaine durant les années U14 et U15. Il a rejoint l'ASSE cet été, repéré par le duo de scouts stéphanois dans le bassin francilien, Mahamadou Gory et Hamdane Karouni. A l'ASSE, il n'est même pas passé par la case U16 et a intégré immédiatement les U17 de David Le Moal, comptant 8 titularisations, 3 entrées en jeu.

Marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg has taken advantage of the early cold snap to smash the world one-hour record for skating on natural ice.

The 29-year-old took to the ice in Winterswijk, Gelderland, at 8.30am on Tuesday and covered a distance of 34 kilometres 878 metres, beating the previous women’s record by 2.6 kilometres.

“I could feel my legs and my back hurting at the end, but there were so many people standing on the sidelines that it gave me energy,” she told NOS.

The previous record, set four years ago by Femke Mossinkoff, also in Winterswijk, was the first official time for the hour by a woman on natural ice. On the same day Bart Vreugdenhil set the current men’s record of 36 kilometers 717 metres.

Most skating records are set on artificial ice, but Winterswijk is one of three arenas where the local club has been able to create a natural arena for early-morning skaters during the recent cold weather.

The all-time women’s record is 40 kilometres 569 metres, set by another Dutch skater, Carien Kleibeuker, in Inzell, Austria, in 2015.

The rink at Winterswijk closed a few hours after Krabbenborg’s record-breaking skate as the ice started to melt, but it is expected to be available again on Wednesday morning.

La réserve a écrasé ce mercredi 4-0 la faible équipe de Hope Team, sélection de joueurs chinois évoluant sous le maillot de l'AJA et dans le groupe A du Challenge Espoirs, où elle affiche un 0 pointé avec 0 but marqué et 18 buts encaissés en 3 matches dont 10 inscrits par Monaco, 4 par le VAFC et 4 par le Paris FC.

Sources indicate that ce match amical aura permis à Sylvain Gibert de donner du temps de jeu à des garçons qui en avaient besoin. Y ont pris part des réservistes, des U19, des U17, un U16 (le néo-international Izaya Kimpioka) mais aussi 3 joueurs à l'essai qui se sont montrés décisifs.

It has been revealed that C'est d'ailleurs sur un coup de pied arrêté tiré par l'un d'entre eux que Mamadou Kanté a ouvert le score une minute avant la mi-temps. Sur un ballon en profondeur d'un deuxième joueur à l'essai, Tidiane Vibert, expulsé dimanche dernier avec les U19 sur le terrain du Cavigal, s'est bien racheté en inscrivant le but du break en début de seconde période.

Mamadou Konté a ôté tout espoir à Hope Team d'un nouveau coup de tête imparable sur un corner de Lenny Marliac. Sur un centre de Noham Akil, le U17 Timothé Demassieux a clôturé le score d'une frappe légèrement déviée par un Chinois au ras du poteau.

La compo : R.Fuleki - Cheikh (c), Benkou, Assoumani (Lengi, 70'), joueur à l'essai (Marliac, 60') - Thouilleux (Demassieux, 46'), Akil, joueur à l'essai (Kimpioka, 60'), Vibert (O.Mendy, 75') - Joueur à l'essai (Freychet, 70'), Konte.

L'ex centrale biancoceleste promuove il percorso della squadra: idee sul campo, muro arretrato, maturazione di Rino e orizzonti più ampi.

In a recent development, angelo Gregucci, ex difensore biancoceleste e storico collaboratore di Roberto Mancini, è stato intervistato dal Corriere della Sera (edizione Roma). Ha analizzato il percorso della Lazio toccando piano partita, difesa, crescita di Gattuso e ambizioni.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Con il Milan, una delle due partite che non ha vinto, il piano partita era perfetto. Mi sembra innovativo, tanti con lui sono migliorati. È un tecnico esigente. So che chiede molto pure a massaggiatori, fisioterapisti e altri. Il merito è suo? Mi sembra evidente. Ha migliorato qualsiasi comparto: comunicazione, campo... Ha cambiato lo status delle cose. Rino non è più solo l'uomo grintoso che investe tutte le energie in ogni allenamento, arrivando a giocare con calciatori tecnicamente più forti di lui. Oggi, attraverso esperienze anche in campionati e piazze che molti avrebbero snobbato, è diventato una guida.

Recent findings suggest that partiti Gila e Romagnoli, sembrava non si potesse più giocare. Al loro posto non è arrivato Paolo Maldini. Eppure la Lazio ha la miglior difesa del torneo.

Quel giorno in molti temevano la retrocessione. Personalmente a inizio campionato pensavo che la Lazio sarebbe potuta arrivare fra il sesto e l'ottavo posto. Oggi però mi sembra competitiva per qualsiasi traguardo.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:25 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 17:35 EST, 21 November 2026.

Wouter Vrancken mentioned Hearts’ ruthless 8-0 demolition of 10-man Dundee was his team’s best performance since he took charge at Tynecastle.

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kabore both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal taking the tally to eight without reply.

And Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style.

Sources indicate that the 47-year-old stated: 'The best performance? Of course.

'When you have the confidence of one moment and then you feel the score is getting bigger, you see the players with extra confidence.

'You see the dynamics there and it’s good they feel it works.

Stuart Findlay heads in the eighth to cap a remarkable evening for Hearts at Dens Park.

'When it’s 0-0 and 1-0, you don’t feel as confident so maybe you don’t have the bravery to do it or show it.

'Today they did it and hopefully they felt it can work and they can show it more.

'It was ruthless and I like to see it this way. That was the message at half-time – that and keeping the clean sheet.

'I was very happy with the performance, not only the score.

'We had the talks before our days off, they were really honest and open. It was good to hear but you have to take ownership of it on the pitch.

'You can talk as much as you want but if you can’t show it on the pitch it doesn’t mean anything.

'When you do it like this it’s the first step.

'But it’s only the first step, only one game and we have to try to bring more.

“The message to the players is feet back on the ground because after the last break we started with a 5-0 win over St Mirren then had difficult moments.

'It was ruthless in the game today but the schedule is also ruthless – but we got a good boost from tonight.'.

Claudio Braga fires home a fifth goal for Vrancken's side in the demolition job.

Dundee boss Steven Pressley admitted he was embarrassed by the result and performance.

He said: 'It’s a night I need to own, a night where I can only apologise for the performance. I never expected that.

'I had a little sense we haven’t been quite on it over the last couple of weeks but I take ownership and I mean that.

'We talk about the culture and environment that we set and part of that is making sure we have a fully motivated team, a team which works hard and shows grit.

'We didn’t show that tonight but that is on me and I mean that.

'We looked unmotivated and lacking edge tonight.

'Tactically astute, we were miles away and that’s my responsibility.

'All areas of our performance was disappointing.

'I’m embarrassed by it and I accept it.'.

L'ancien Vert, Mathys Saban opère désormais au Mâcon 71 (N2), après un passage au Luxembourg (Titus Petange, Racing FC Union). Au sortir d’une crise interne marquée par une grève de l’entraînement, Mâcon 71 jouait un match important sur le terrain de la réserve d'Annecy. À dix contre onze (après l'exclusion de l'ancien Vert, Israël Kinunga) et après avoir été rattrapé sur penalty, les Mâconnais ont montré qu’ils savaient réagir. C'est Mathys Saban, entré en jeu à la 71ème, qui a donné la victoire (1-2) aux siens, à la toute dernière minute du match. Un autre ancien Vert, Yoann Greco est entré en jeu à la 65ème.Avec 11 points, Mäcon 71 pointe à la 7ème place, à 8 points du leader Bourgoin dans le championnat de N2.

Mathys Saban (24 ans), joueur offensif polyvalent, est arrivé au centre de Formation de l'ASSE en 2017, en provenance de l'US Torcy qui a fourni aux Verts Lamine Ghezali, Alexandre Valbon, Josué Gago et Marwan Nzuzi, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Mathis Amougou, Fodé Camara, Axel Dodote. Il a gravi toutes les étapes de la formation et signé son premier contrat pro de 3 ans avec l'ASSE le 5 juin 2020, contrat qui sera prolongé de 2 ans en février 2023.En 2020-2021, il joue son premier match en pro, le 23 mai 2021, 12 minutes lors de ASSE-Dijon : 0-1.En 2021-2022, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 1 : - 21 août 2021, 21 minutes : ASSE-LOSC : 1-1- 28 août 2021 : 19 minutes : OM-ASSE : 3-1- 12 septembre 2021 : 30 minutes : Montpellier-ASSE : 2-0En 2022-2023, il participe à 3 matchs de Ligue 2 qui se soldent par 3 défaites, et 1 match en Coupe de France : - le 29 octobre 2022, Coupe de France, 30 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-0 (3-4 tab)- le 7 novembre 2022, 45 minutes, Metz-ASSE : 3-2- le 12 novembre 2022, 17 minutes : ASSE-Rodez : 0-2  - le 26 décembre 2022, 33 minutes : Annecy-ASSE : 2-1.

Le 31 août 2023, il est prêté au club luxembourgeois de l'Union Titus Petange pour la saison 2023-2024. Victime d’une rupture du tendon d’achille au début du printemps 2024 lors de son prêt à l’Union Titus Pétange, Mathys Saban revient à l'ASSE pour la saison 2024-2025 mais ne joue que 77 minutes en N3 pour sa 8ème et dernière saison sous le maillot vert. Il retourne  dans le Grand-Duché durant l'été 2025 (au Racing Football Club Union Lëtzebuerg), et inscrit en septembre 2025 son premier but en L1 luxembourgeoise. Malheureusement son contrat est rompu début 2026 et, après 6 mois sans club, il rejoint donc le Mâcon 71 qui a raté de peu l'accession au Championnat National, devancé par Hauts Lyonnais.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

PSV and Feyenoord face an uphill task to reach the group stages of the Champions League after defeats on Tuesday night saw them drop out of the qualifying places.

PSV briefly threatened to cause an upset in Madrid as they took a 1-0 lead into the half-time break. Ivan Perisic’s penalty after 32 minutes was their only reward for a courageous first-half display in which Ruben van Bommel and Sven Mijnans also missed clear chances to score.

According to recent reports, but the introduction of Jude Bellingham at half-time changed the picture as Real’s superstars regrouped to score five goals. The England midfielder’s dazzling volley was the pick of the bunch, while Kylian Mbappé bagged a double and Vinicius Junior also got on the scoresheet.

Head coach Peter Bosz admitted his team had been “trampled underfoot” in the second half. “I think you had to be there to see how substantial the difference was between the first and second half,” he noted.

“In the first half we were brave, put our opponents under pressure and had three big chances in the first four minutes.

In a recent development, “When you look at the second half, they scored quickly and the tempo of their game was much higher. That’s the quality they have with the players they can bring off the bench.”.

PSV’s next match is a home tie against Real’s city rivals Atletico on December 9, before they travel to Stavanger to take on Viking in January and round off the group stage at home to Stuttgart.

Feyenoord suffered a narrower defeat at home to Porto as they were unable to recover from an own goal after two minutes by Oussama Targhalline.

Goalkeeper Florian Kastenmeier vindicated the decision of Giovanni van Bronckhorst to replace the out-of-form Tjark Ernst by making some vital saves to keep the Rotterdammers in the game.

Feyenoord staged a late rally, with Gjivai Zechiël going close and Targhalline striking the crossbar from long range, but they were unable to breach the Portuguese side’s defence.

The fans in De Kuip were briefly celebrating after a bizarre incident when referee Irfan Peltjo’s watch told him a header by Nacho Ferri had crossed the line, but video replays clearly highlighted it bounced off the post and into the hands of Diogo Costa.

In a recent development, feyenoord have just three points from their five matches so far, one less than PSV. Their next two matches are away to Viking on December 8 and Galatasaray on January 19, before they close their campaign in Rotterdam against RB Leipzig.

Industry News: MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.
  • Industry observers note that and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

Industry observers note that and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

According to recent reports, balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It has been revealed that it looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

Messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

That’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers.

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top.

However, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up substantial-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

In a recent development, jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

In a recent development, it was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Recent findings suggest that djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park.

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

Industry observers note that the South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

According to recent reports, an initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

According to recent reports, motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Said, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side.

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

It has been revealed that with Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

Sources indicate that unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It has been revealed that it shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.
