In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Recent findings suggest that alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that C'est une annonce majeure pour le football belge en ce lundi 16 novembre 2026. Sur son compte Instagram, Romelu Lukaku a officialisé son départ définitif de la sélection des Diables Rouges après seize années passées au plus haut niveau international.

L'attaquant de 33 ans a surpris l'ensemble des observateurs au lendemain de la victoire de la Belgique face à l'Italie (4-1) en Ligue des nations, qui a validé la qualification des Diables Rouges pour les quarts de finale du tournoi. Dimanche 15 novembre 2026, Romelu Lukaku est resté sur le banc des remplaçants sans entrer en jeu, après avoir manqué le match précédent face à la Turquie en raison d'une légère blessure à la hanche. Pour accompagner son message d'adieu sur le réseau social, le joueur a publié une galerie photo retraçant son parcours international depuis ses débuts en mars 2010 à l'âge de 16 ans. Plusieurs coéquipiers emblématiques de la génération dorée, dont Axel Witsel et Thibaut Courtois, ont d'ailleurs salué publiquement sa carrière sous sa publication. Une page se tourne pour les Diables Rouges.

En quittant la sélection, Romelu Lukaku laisse un héritage statistique considérable. L'avant-centre se retire en effet en tant que meilleur buteur absolu de l'histoire de la sélection belge avec 94 buts inscrits en 135 sélections. Au niveau des apparitions, le joueur n'est devancé que par Jan Vertonghen (157 sélections) et Axel Witsel (140 sélections). Pilier de la sélection durant plus d'une décennie, il a disputé quatre phases finales de Coupe du monde (2014, 2018 avec une 3e place, 2022 et 2026) ainsi que trois Championnats d'Europe (2016, 2020 et 2024). Son dernier match officiel sous le maillot des Diables Rouges remonte ainsi au 5 octobre 2026 contre l'équipe de France en Ligue des nations, lors d'une défaite (1-4).

Cette annonce constitue d'ailleurs un revirement par rapport aux looks initialement affichés par l'intéressé. En effet, l'attaquant avait affirmé en janvier 2026 que la Coupe du monde 2026 ne marquerait pas sa dernière compétition majeure avec la Belgique. La sélection des Diables Rouges a elle aussi tenu à rendre hommage à son avant-centre sur son compte officiel X, saluant un joueur qui a écrit un incroyable chapitre de l'histoire de l'équipe nationale.

According to recent reports, la situation sportive de l'attaquant s'était toutefois compliquée lors des dernières semaines avec les Diables Rouges. Depuis la prise de fonction de Mark van Bommel comme sélectionneur en août 2026 en remplacement de Rudi Garcia, Romelu Lukaku a vu son temps de jeu diminuer au profit de Charles De Ketelaere. Resté sur le banc lors du récent succès face à l'Italie, le joueur a finalement choisi de renoncer aux prochaines échéances internationales de son pays. En effet, la Belgique disputera les quarts de finale de la Ligue des nations du 25 au 30 mars 2027, dont le tirage au sort est fixé au vendredi 20 novembre 2026 à Nyon.

In a recent development, toutefois, cette retraite internationale ne met absolument pas un terme à sa carrière en club. Romelu Lukaku évolue sous les couleurs de Fenerbahçe depuis le mois d'août 2026 et reste concentré sur ses objectifs en Turquie. L'attaquant disputera ainsi son prochain match officiel le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 17h00 face à Kocaelispor en Süper Lig.

Présent en conférence de presse ce lundi 16 novembre 2026 à Singapour, Vinicius Jr a livré une mise au point sans détour sur ses récentes difficultés avec le Real Madrid. L'attaquant brésilien a admis avoir diminué son volume d'entraînement estival, profondément affecté par l'élimination précoce de sa sélection lors de la dernière Coupe du monde.

Ce début d'exercice s'avère particulièrement difficile pour le joueur de 26 ans sous les couleurs du club espagnol. Avec un bilan de seulement un but et trois passes décisives en 12 rencontres toutes compétitions confondues avec le Real Madrid, Vinicius Jr traverse une période délicate. Un rendement bien loin de ses standards. La cause de ce passage à vide trouve son origine dans les suites de la Coupe du monde, où le Brésil a quitté la compétition dès les huitièmes de finale après une défaite face à la Norvège (2-1). Très affecté par ce revers, l'attaquant a ainsi privilégié le repos et la déconnexion en famille durant ses vacances, au détriment de sa préparation physique.

Devant les médias à Singapour, l'ailier madrilène a d'ailleurs détaillé avec franchise les raisons de ce déficit athlétique :.

Au-delà de cette déception internationale, le contexte extra-sportif n'a pas aidé le joueur du Real Madrid à aborder cette saison l'esprit totalement libéré. En effet, le dossier de sa prolongation contractuelle et les sollicitations extérieures, notamment l'intérêt de clubs comme Arsenal, ont perturbé sa concentration estivale. L'attaquant a ainsi reconnu que ces remous avaient directement influé sur son niveau de jeu depuis la reprise.

Industry observers note that toutefois, l'ailier madrilène a tenu à rappeler la difficulté de se maintenir au sommet dans la durée. Pour appuyer son constat, il a souligné que seuls Cristiano Ronaldo et Lionel Messi ont su afficher de telles statistiques pendant de longues années. Le numéro 7 brésilien a également rappelé son devoir d'exemplarité, affirmant être conscient que s'il court davantage, tous les jeunes joueurs courront aussi plus.

Industry observers note that vinicius Jr a tempéré les inquiétudes en comparant sa trajectoire à celle de la saison passée, où il ne comptait que 5 buts en décembre avant de dépasser la barre des 20 réalisations au printemps. L'attaquant reste ainsi convaincu que sa montée en puissance physique portera ses fruits au moment opportun.

It has been revealed that sur le proposal sportif en sélection, Vinicius Jr s'est d'ailleurs redonné de la confiance en signant un doublé samedi 14 novembre 2026 lors de la défaite du Brésil contre le Japon (2-3) au Stade national de Singapour. Le Brésil dispute désormais son prochain match amical face à Singapour le mardi 17 novembre 2026 à 11h00 (heure française) au Stade national de Singapour. Le prochain rendez-vous de Vinicius Jr avec le Real Madrid est ensuite programmé le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à 21h00 face au Celta Vigo au stade Santiago-Bernabéu pour la 13e journée de Liga.

Bruno Fernandes reveals contract negotiations with Manchester United have stalled after he rejected a new deal in the summer

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed newly introduced deal.
  • The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed newly introduced deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United.

Recent findings suggest that 'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always indicated how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

Sources indicate that 'And I've always stated the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club says "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a new contract so I think that from their side demonstrates that they want me to stay.

'As I stated there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most notable thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'.

It has been revealed that the club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

Industry observers note that united right now sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he notes in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he said.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

According to recent reports, his post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

According to recent reports, 'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he stated. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference.

According to recent reports, 'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

In a recent development, 'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

Industry observers note that 'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

In a recent development, la prudenza dipende dalla natura dello stop. Davide Frattesi era stato rimandato a casa dal ritiro della Nazionale per un affaticamento; Zaccagni, invece, ha dovuto superare una lesione al quadricipite. Una nuova risonanza magnetica, effettuata la settimana scorsa, aveva mostrato un miglioramento dell’edema post-traumatico.

Adesso l’edema si è completamente riassorbito e il capitano è disponibile. La Lazio, però, non vuole correre rischi, anche in vista degli impegni di dicembre. Gattuso deciderà soltanto alla vigilia se utilizzarlo dall’inizio contro il Torino.

It has been revealed that anche Nuno Tavares guarda a un appuntamento preciso: il derby del 13 dicembre. Il portoghese procede lentamente e non ha ancora ripreso ad allenarsi con il gruppo. Per avvicinarsi al rientro dovrà accelerare il lavoro nei prossimi giorni.

According to recent reports, restano incerti i tempi di recupero di Marusic. Il problema nella zona del tendine, accusato durante il ritiro con il Montenegro, non consente ancora di stabilire quando tornerà. È il suo terzo stop stagionale. It has been revealed that luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

According to recent reports, 'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

Recent findings suggest that asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

It has been revealed that you make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

There has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke.

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

It has been revealed that belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

It has been revealed that williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' stated Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

Recent findings suggest that spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

According to recent reports, savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. In a recent development, guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. “But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Recent findings suggest that raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

Zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the newly introduced £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

In a recent development, in the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he said.

Sources indicate that the key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Industry observers note that hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

“I love those challenges,” remarked Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

It has been revealed that arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026.

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was announced as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title.

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched.

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021.

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

Il presidente della Lazio punta a tornare nell’incarico; per i tre posti si presentano anche gli uscenti e Sticchi Damiani.

Industry observers note that la Serie A eleggerà tre consiglieri federali il 14 dicembre, ma i candidati sono cinque. Ai tre uscenti Stefano Campoccia, Giorgio Chiellini e Giuseppe Marotta si sono aggiunti Saverio Sticchi Damiani e il presidente della Lazio Claudio Lotito. Tra le ipotesi in vista del voto c’è anche quella di preferenze disgiunte tra la presidenza FIGC e il Consiglio federale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nel breve mandato di Malagò, i posti spettanti alla massima serie erano occupati da Campoccia, dell’Udinese, Chiellini, della Juventus, e Marotta, dell’Inter. Tutti e tre si sono ricandidati. Con loro correranno il presidente del Lecce Sticchi Damiani e Lotito, che punta a tornare nell’incarico già ricoperto.

Come riferisce il Corriere dello Sport, il quadro delle candidature si inserisce in una Serie A attraversata da divisioni. Alcuni club sono usciti dal fronte Malagò, con Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra gli indecisi figurano anche Juventus e Milan; in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali, le fratture interne potrebbero allargarsi.

Sources indicate that ogni società di Serie A può indicare un candidato al Consiglio federale. Nelle precedenti elezioni Chiellini aveva ottenuto sette voti e Marotta sei, in una situazione descritta come praticamente opposta a quella attuale.

It has been revealed that il fronte favorevole a Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista Marotta, potrebbe risentire della propria posizione di minoranza. I club che sostengono Malagò sono almeno 11: un sostegno necessario alla sua candidatura, per la quale serve l’appoggio di almeno una componente.

In questo scenario, alcune società potrebbero scegliere il voto disgiunto: sostenere un candidato alla presidenza FIGC e, per il Consiglio federale, esprimere una preferenza per un nome non apertamente schierato con lui. L’esempio indicato è un voto per Malagò alla presidenza e per Marotta, primo sostenitore di Galliani, come consigliere. Una soluzione che richiederebbe un lavoro diplomatico.

Napoli star Scott McTominay and his girlfriend Cam Reading have announced they're expecting their first child together.

The couple shared a joint post on Instagram with one picture of them holding up an ultrasound image, another of Reading reclining in a bikini and a third of the pregnancy test itself.

They revealed the news on the same day McTominay broke Napoli's three-game losing streak, scoring the winner in a 1-0 victory over Torino.

The couple wrote: 'The most precious gift, a lifetime of love.' McTominay, 29, and Reading have settled into life in Italy after he joined from Man United and revived his career, winning the Scudetto and earning Player of the Year honours.

It remains to be seen whether the baby will be born in Italy or back in the UK but the couple were overjoyed at sharing their happy news.

It is not exactly clear when McTominay and Reading first crossed paths but they have at least been together since the summer of 2023, when they were pictured on a boat trip in Greece.

Cam Reading and Scott McTominay shared the news that they're expecting a baby.

Reading posted this picture of her bump on her Instagram page and wrote of a 'precious gift'.

Reading, a director at asset management firm Fortress Capital partners, has seen her personal celebrity skyrocket in that time, zooming up from 10,000 Instagram followers to over 90,000.

According to La Repubblica, they have moved into a house by Lago Patria, a coastal lake near the suburb of Giugliano.

There, McTominay can be by the seaside rapidly after popping out of his door and is only around a 20-minute drive from Napoli's training centre.

The couple regularly share photos from their new life together in Italy and McTominay is adored by fans having repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the 2024-25 season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

Recent findings suggest that this season has been less straightforward for McTominay. The Scotland international underwent heart surgery after being diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and he was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli, scoring the winner against Torino on Saturday.

McTominay and Reading also posted this snap of the ultrasound and positive test.

The midfielder scored the winner on Saturday for Napoli against Torino.

He has now scored 33 goals in 92 matches across all competitions with the Partenopei and remains one of Serie A's leading lights.

The Italian press gushed over his contribution on Saturday, with Corriere dello Sport writing: 'He played with fire in his belly.

'Three shots in the opening 16 minutes; seven in total—three on target— and a decisive goal (his fourth against Torino, his favourite Serie A opponent, along with Inter), plus the charisma of a leader.'.

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6142 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent major players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

They hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Sources indicate that afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

Sources indicate that it was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

Industry observers note that the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

There was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

And the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the issue then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

United can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very vital in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

In a recent development, it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

Sources indicate that with Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La campagna coinvolge sei calciatori e calciatrici delle Nazionali e rinnova l’invito a comporre il 1522.

Sources indicate that la FIGC rinnova il suo impegno contro la violenza sulle donne con una campagna di sensibilizzazione affidata a sei calciatori e calciatrici e ribadisce l’invito alle vittime di violenza o stalking a chiamare il 1522. Secondo quanto riportato da Figc, L’iniziativa è legata alla Giornata internazionale per l’eliminazione della violenza sulle donne. Lo riferisce la FIGC.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that gianluigi Donnarumma, Cristiana Girelli, Laura Giuliani, Pio Esposito, Riccardo Calafiori e Annamaria Serturini sono i protagonisti della comunicazione della Federazione. La campagna affronta la violenza di genere in tutte le sue forme: non soltanto gli episodi di cronaca, ancora troppo frequenti, ma anche la dimensione culturale e sociale del fenomeno, legata agli stereotipi e al mancato riconoscimento della libertà e dell’autonomia delle donne.

Il messaggio distingue la violenza da ciò che può essere presentato come una lite, il controllo dalla gelosia e il possesso dalla protezione: «È una lite? No, è violenza. È gelosia? No, è controllo. È protezione? No, è possesso». A queste domande la campagna affianca una risposta: il numero 1522.

Recent findings suggest that il 1522 è un servizio gratuito di pubblica utilità istituito nel 2006 dal Dipartimento per le Pari Opportunità. Il suo obiettivo è favorire l’emersione e il contrasto della violenza contro le donne, sia all’interno sia all’esterno della famiglia, attraverso un’ampia azione di sistema.

In occasione della Giornata internazionale, la FIGC torna quindi a invitare le vittime di ogni forma di violenza o stalking a comporre il numero.

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Luke McCowan's timely return to form silences Parkhead critics and boosts midfield options

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1265 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 11:58 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 12:18 EST, 22 November 2026.

Almost everyone who has played the game of football at a professional level has experienced a day where they simply can’t do right for doing wrong.

When one heavy touch leads to another and each decision made seems worse than the last one.

Like the buses in his native Greenock, it was Luke McCowan’s misfortune for two such traumatic experiences to arrive in close proximity.

His inept performance as a substitute on a dark night for Celtic in Linz in August will flash through his mind when he’s old and grey.

Handed the opportunity to atone for it with a start in the league game against Rangers at Parkhead the following month, his withdrawal at half-time felt like an act of mercy.

According to recent reports, A Celtic supporter all his days, McCowan didn’t have to speak to articulate the depth of his despair in that trying time. Subjected to a barrage of online criticism, the deletion of his social media accounts said enough.

Luke McCowan scored in the 4-1 home victory over St Mirren.

Skipper Callum McGregor and McCowan enjoy the victory at full-time.

While you could understand why the midfielder would have felt personally responsible for a pair of high-profile losses, there was a lot more to the team’s shortcomings on those occasions than one man performing as if his laces were tied together.

Away to LASK, Celtic were already wilting when he shed his tracksuit. He didn’t stop the slide towards an extraordinary exit from the Champions League but he didn’t instigate it.

At home to Rangers, Celtic were flat and second-best from the outset and remained that way even after McCowan came inside for the second period.

Industry observers note that the 28-year-old was not alone in failing to do himself justice on those occasions and in other matches around what was a difficult period for Martin O’Neill’s side. It might just have felt like it.

As shown by his contributions to a side who were capable of winning the title in his first two seasons in Glasgow, McCowan was – and is – a far more accomplished player than those unfortunate episodes suggested.

It has been revealed that he wasn’t the first and he won’t be the last player to suffer a crisis of confidence. And despite being no shrinking violet, he would not be human if those experiences didn’t shake him up and lead him to question if he was worthy of wearing the jersey that he always dreamed of.

His display on Saturday should have emphatically answered those inner doubts.

Trusted by his manager to fill the void created by the injury to Mika Baur, McCowan delivered.

According to recent reports, even before he scored to put the game to bed just before half-time, he played smart passes, made intelligent runs and made key interceptions. He looked very much a Celtic player again.

McGregor takes the acclaim from team-mates after scoring Celtic's fourth goal.

No one in O’Neill’s side, in fact, did more to ensure that they went up the tunnel at the interval to warm applause.

With Baur’s absence for up to ten weeks already a source of stress to the Celtic manager, Benjamin Nygren’s sore heel would have further disrupted his sleep on Friday night.

Saturday proved to be quite the day for O’Neill’s fringe men, though.

On top of McCowan’s assured display, we witnessed Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain serve up a reminder of why he once wore the jerseys of Arsenal, Liverpool and England.

In a recent development, playing deeper than McCowan, Oxlade-Chamberlain stretched St Mirren with his pinpoint passing, long and short. He kept the ball in tight areas and made it all look so simple.

He was in the right place at the right time to stroke home Yang Hyun-jun’s cut-back to put his side in front and never put a foot wrong until his legs could give no more.

The cherry on the cake for O’Neill came by way of Joel van den Berg’s debut from the bench.

Having seen the club shell out over £3million to PSV Eindhoven, Celtic supporters were growing a little concerned that the teenager hadn’t yet featured for the first team.

Now fully recovered from an injury, he belatedly caught the eye. Tall, skilful and rangy, he looked the part. Might he have earned himself a call-up to the Europa League squad as a replacement for Baur? You would not be surprised.

Celtic will certainly travel to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday in optimistic mood after making short work of seeing off the Buddies.

Arriving just before McCowan turned home Kieran Tierney’s cross, Camilo Duran claimed his 14th of the season by bundling in a brilliant assist from the same source. Stationed on the bench throughout, Kasper Hogh wasn’t even afforded a chance to end his 16-game goal drought.

On a good day for a makeshift midfield, Callum McGregor, its mainstay, claimed Celtic’s fourth with a controlled strike after the break.

Industry observers note that sam Johnstone didn’t have a great deal to do, testament to Celtic’s work without the ball. Tierney was excellent for 71 minutes, despite playing the entirety of Scotland’s games with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The directness and industry of Yang on the right flank was also eye-catching. Omitted from the squad for the second successive match, Haissem Hassan will surely have taken note.

On the other flank, Jota looked like a player who’s threatening to really fire again.

Industry observers note that A late run-out for Auston Trusty, the first since the death of his father, was met by warm applause by home fans. O’Neill will certainly need the American in the coming weeks.

While Killian Phillips did spoil Johnstone’s clean sheet by converting a penalty which the keeper gave away, O’Neill would have had few complaints about a display which saw his side create an abundance of opportunities.

According to recent reports, it must be stated that St Mirren were their own worst enemies. They are proving to be a strange fish under Craig McLeish. Even in defeat, some of their football on Saturday was eye-catching.

Yet again, though, they showed themselves to be a soft touch defensively. They were fortunate not to ship more than four and it’s hardly a new thing, either.

The Buddies haven’t kept a clean sheet since winning by a goal at Rugby Park on September 2. In the ten subsequent matches, they’ve picked the ball out of their net 23 times. It’s becoming a real concern.

While they are more creative and entertaining than when Stephen Robinson was in charge, they could badly do with becoming as hard to beat as they were under their former boss.

According to recent reports, they are now just five points above Kilmarnock ahead of their meeting in Paisley this weekend. That would be an opportune moment for it all to come together.

It has been revealed that CELTIC (4-3-2-1): Johnstone 6.5; Donovan 7, Carter-Vickers 7, Scales 7, Tierney 7.5 (Trusty 70); McGregor 7, OXLADE- CHAMBERLAIN 8 (Osmand 60), McCowan 7.5; Yang 7 (Forrest 70), Duran 7 (Mheuka 70); Jota 6.5 (Van den Berg 60). Booked: McCowan. Manager: Martin O’Neill 7.

Sources indicate that ST MIRREN: (4-2-3-1) Chapman 5; Ramsay 5, Jackson 5, Gogic 5, John 4; Carr 6 (Donnelly 84), Nsio 5.5 (Taylor 85); Thomas 5 (Young 65), Phillips 5.5 (Ramos 74), Kabia 5; Sule 5 (Mochrie 65). Booked: Gogic. Manager: Craig McLeish 4.

La Lazio si prepara a ritrovare i suoi tifosi: circa 40mila sono attesi all’Olimpico per il derby del 13 dicembre e altri 20mila a Milano per la Supercoppa contro l’Inter, in programma il 22 dicembre. Per Gattuso il ritorno del pubblico nello stadio di casa riguarda, almeno, le sfide con l’Atalanta e con la Roma.

Per la stracittadina sono previsti circa 40mila laziali all’Olimpico. La previsione per la Supercoppa contro l’Inter è invece di 20mila tifosi a Milano. Nella gara del 22 dicembre la Lazio proverà a conquistare il diciassettesimo trofeo della sua storia.

Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

📅 14 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5335 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half.
  • Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins.
  • There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, stated. “But this was a top-class performance.”.

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

Recent findings suggest that "He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj.

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous latest West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a significant evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Sources indicate that major? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Sources indicate that leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

According to recent reports, ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO.

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9.

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x.

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

Industry observers note that “That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”.

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

In a recent development, [It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have remarked it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No.

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

Recent findings suggest that it’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Recent findings suggest that regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

According to recent reports, but Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

In a recent development, jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their upcoming model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

It has been revealed that joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who indicates that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

Tuur Rommens has urged his Rangers team-mates to use a breakneck run of three home games in eight days to build a platform from which to launch a real assault on the Premiership title.

Derek McInnes’ side play host to Aberdeen on Tuesday and then have Falkirk and Dundee United visiting – with Belgian left-back Rommens clear on the need to use the Ibrox atmosphere as a weapon.

‘At the away games, there’s a lot of fans, but at home there’s even more, so it gives an extra boost,’ he said.

‘I think, at home, we have to maintain our good run.

‘We’ll try to keep on winning these three games and then we’ll see from there. If you keep winning, you’ll be up there.

‘We’re back to Ibrox (on Tuesday) and it’s been a long time, but, yeah, it’s nice to play in front of our fans again.

Tuur Rommens (right) celebrates with match-winner Ryan Naderi at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed home the opener in Rangers' 2-1 victory at Motherwell.

‘I guess Aberdeen, it’s a difficult one, but we’ll try to keep on winning.’.

Rangers dug out a crucial 2-1 win at Motherwell on Saturday thanks to an 88th-minute Ryan Naderi winner and sit four points behind leaders Celtic with a game in hand.

Rommens believes the side’s ability to pull wins out of the fire and show they are willing to keep pushing right to the end of matches is helping build unity within the squad and with their followers.

‘Yeah, exactly,’ he said. ‘Also with the fans, when you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they’re so happy, we’re so happy, so it gives us extra boost to go on Tuesday again and try to get a win.

‘I think the fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn’t feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us.

In a recent development, ‘Especially for the newly introduced guys, that’s new. It’s the same for me. I’m not even here one year so I’m getting surprised every time that there are so many fans of Rangers when we’re playing outside.’.

Rommens also took time to lavish praise on Naderi and revealed what a deeply loved figure the Czech international has become within the dressing room.

Asked about the progress Naderi has made with his game in recent months, he replied: ‘It’s unbelievable.

‘You can always give the ball to him and he just keeps it.

Industry observers note that ‘He’s very strong and I think he deserves all these goals that he gets. So yeah, I’m very happy for him.

According to recent reports, ‘He delivers, he scores a lot of goals, he gives assists, so everybody’s happy for him and he’s a good guy. Everybody loves him in the group.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A Roma, il capitano della Lazio incontra gli alunni della scuola primaria Pistelli vincitrice del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”. Tra gioco, movimento e storie personali, un messaggio: nello sport, come nella vita, la ver.

Sources indicate that ROMA – Gol al novantesimo o weekend senza compiti? Derby vinto o 10 in matematica? Questa volta la sfida si gioca tra i banchi di scuola e a scendere in campo è Mattia Zaccagni. Il capitano della Lazio incontra i bambini della Scuola Primaria Pistelli di Roma per una partita speciale a colpi di “Questo o quello?”, tra domande a sorpresa, risposte istintive e qualche scelta davvero difficile.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that L’appuntamento fa parte del percorso nazionale promosso da Sport e Salute e adidas per contrastare il drop-out sportivo e tenere viva, fin dai primi anni, la voglia di fare sport. E la Pistelli non è una scuola qualsiasi: istituto aderente a Scuola Attiva Kids, è stata protagonista del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”, conquistando il primo posto grazie al percorso realizzato per promuovere il movimento come parte integrante della quotidianità scolastica. Una comunità che ha scelto di fare dello sport un’abitudine, un’opportunità e un’esperienza da condividere.

Sources indicate that È proprio da questa energia che prende vita l’incontro con Zaccagni. I bambini diventano arbitri delle scelte, mentre il campione si mette alla prova: gol decisivo o vacanza più lunga? Una partita vinta o un bel voto a scuola? Ma dietro le risate e le risposte più divertenti c’è anche spazio per qualcosa di più profondo. Perché lo sport non è soltanto il momento della vittoria: è imparare a gestire una sconfitta, superare un errore, affrontare una difficoltà e trovare ogni volta la voglia di ripartire.

«Nel calcio, come nella vita, ci sono momenti in cui le cose non vanno come vorresti. Puoi sbagliare un gol, perdere una partita o attraversare un periodo complicato. Ma è proprio in quei momenti che devi trovare la forza di rialzarti, continuare a lavorare e credere nelle tue capacità. Io ho imparato che non si cresce soltanto quando si vince, ma soprattutto quando si riesce a reagire alle difficoltà. Ai ragazzi dico di divertirsi, di non avere paura di sbagliare e di non mollare mai quello che li fa stare bene. Perché nello sport, prima ancora dei risultati, conta la voglia di continuare a giocare», racconta Mattia Zaccagni ai bambini.

Dalle parole si passa al movimento. Con i tutor di Sport e Salute, gli alunni partecipano a una lezione di attività motoria, tra giochi, prove di abilità e lavoro di squadra. Tutti protagonisti, ciascuno con le proprie capacità, in un’esperienza che mette al centro il piacere di muoversi e stare insieme.

Industry observers note that È questa la sfida che Sport e Salute e adidas vogliono vincere: contrastare l’abbandono sportivo, offrendo ai più giovani occasioni per scoprire una passione, sentirsi parte di una squadra e trovare nello sport uno spazio in cui crescere. Perché nessuno dovrebbe smettere di giocare solo perché non è il più bravo, perché ha incontrato una difficoltà o perché una partita è andata male.

La Pistelli, con il suo percorso premiato a livello nazionale, dimostra che questa partita può iniziare proprio dalla scuola. E che il risultato più importante non è segnare un gol in più, ma fare in modo che domani ci siano ancora tanti bambini pronti a scendere in campo.
